# No Wire Leaves Cordova. So the Load Moved In.

> What does Cordova do with power it can't sell and can't ship out?

Published 2026-08-12 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-08-12/

## The story

Nothing leaves Cordova by wire.

The amount landed August 11th. $725,000.

The nearest line is 56 km away.

A fifth of it goes nowhere.

Twenty feet from the turbine.

Greensparc put 170 kilowatts of computing inside the Humpback Creek run of river plant, several miles north of town. The National Laboratory of the Rockies reported it in March. (C18, C26)

The whole co-op, to scale.

Over 200 island grids. One got picked.

UAF counts over 200 remote microgrids in Alaska. Each one is a closed loop with nothing joining it to the next. Cordova is one of them. (C06)

The money is not for the data center.

On August 11th UAF published both. $725,000, AURORA-AI, Alaska Utility Resilience and Optimization using Real-time AI, with Richard Wies as principal investigator. It combines utility data, virtual replicas of the power grid and AI to forecast demand and detect abnormal operating conditions. (C01, C02, C03, C05, C07)

## What we verified

- The University of Alaska Fairbanks received a $725,000 award from the U.S. Department of Energy for the AURORA-AI project. [University of Alaska Fairbanks](https://www.uaf.edu/news/uaf-leads-ai-project-to-strengthen-alaskas-rural-power-grids.php), primary document, 2026-08-11.
- AURORA-AI stands for Alaska Utility Resilience and Optimization using Real-time AI. [University of Alaska Fairbanks](https://www.uaf.edu/news/uaf-leads-ai-project-to-strengthen-alaskas-rural-power-grids.php), primary document, 2026-08-11.
- Richard Wies is the principal investigator for AURORA-AI. [University of Alaska Fairbanks](https://www.uaf.edu/news/uaf-leads-ai-project-to-strengthen-alaskas-rural-power-grids.php), primary document, 2026-08-11.
- AURORA-AI is a partnership of the UAF Alaska Center for Energy and Power, Colorado State University, the National Laboratory of the Rockies and Cordova Electric Cooperative. [University of Alaska Fairbanks](https://www.uaf.edu/news/uaf-leads-ai-project-to-strengthen-alaskas-rural-power-grids.php), primary document, 2026-08-11.
- UAF says AURORA-AI will combine high-resolution utility data, virtual replicas of the power grid and AI to forecast demand, detect abnormal operating conditions and optimize energy resources. [University of Alaska Fairbanks](https://www.uaf.edu/news/uaf-leads-ai-project-to-strengthen-alaskas-rural-power-grids.php), primary document, 2026-08-11.
- UAF says Alaska has over 200 remote microgrids. [University of Alaska Fairbanks](https://www.uaf.edu/news/uaf-leads-ai-project-to-strengthen-alaskas-rural-power-grids.php), primary document, 2026-08-11.
- UAF published the AURORA-AI release on August 11th, 2026. [University of Alaska Fairbanks](https://www.uaf.edu/news/uaf-leads-ai-project-to-strengthen-alaskas-rural-power-grids.php), primary document, 2026-08-11.
- The Alaska Center for Energy and Power published its own AURORA-AI release on the same day, August 11th, 2026. [Alaska Center for Energy and Power, University of Alaska Fairbanks](https://www.uaf.edu/acep/news/2026/uaf-leads-ai-project-to-strengthen-alaskas-rural-power-grids.php), primary document, 2026-08-11.
- Richard Wies said Alaska's isolated power systems provide an ideal environment for developing and testing next-generation technologies that can improve electric grid resilience. [University of Alaska Fairbanks](https://www.uaf.edu/news/uaf-leads-ai-project-to-strengthen-alaskas-rural-power-grids.php), primary document, 2026-08-11.
- The AURORA-AI award was made under the U.S. Department of Energy's Genesis Mission. [University of Alaska Fairbanks](https://www.uaf.edu/news/uaf-leads-ai-project-to-strengthen-alaskas-rural-power-grids.php), primary document, 2026-08-11.
- The Department of Energy selected 278 projects in the first Genesis Mission round. [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/articles/secretary-energy-chris-wright-announces-first-genesis-mission-projects-selected-accelerate), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- Of the first round Genesis Mission projects, 168 are led by universities. [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/articles/secretary-energy-chris-wright-announces-first-genesis-mission-projects-selected-accelerate), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- The first Genesis Mission round spans 342 participating institutions including 16 national laboratories and 142 universities. [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/articles/secretary-energy-chris-wright-announces-first-genesis-mission-projects-selected-accelerate), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- The Department of Energy announced the first selected Genesis Mission projects on July 22nd, 2026. [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/articles/secretary-energy-chris-wright-announces-first-genesis-mission-projects-selected-accelerate), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- The $293 million Genesis Mission figure is the size of the Request for Application announced on March 17th, 2026 and the Department of Energy does not state it as the combined value of the 278 selected projects. [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/articles/energy-department-announces-293-million-funding-support-genesis-mission-national-science), primary document, 2026-03-17.
- Genesis Mission Phase I awards range from $500,000 to $750,000 and support a nine month project period. [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/articles/energy-department-announces-293-million-funding-support-genesis-mission-national-science), primary document, 2026-03-17.
- The $725,000 AURORA-AI award falls inside the published Genesis Mission Phase I band of $500,000 to $750,000. [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/articles/energy-department-announces-293-million-funding-support-genesis-mission-national-science), primary document, 2026-03-17.
- Greensparc delivered 170 kilowatts of computing capacity inside Cordova's run of river Humpback Creek hydroelectric facility. [National Laboratory of the Rockies](https://www.nlr.gov/news/detail/program/2026/in-alaska-a-data-center-inside-a-power-plant-inside-a-microgrid), primary document, 2026-03-05.
- In 2025 hydropower provided more than 83 percent of Cordova's overall electrical demand. [National Laboratory of the Rockies](https://www.nlr.gov/news/detail/program/2026/in-alaska-a-data-center-inside-a-power-plant-inside-a-microgrid), primary document, 2026-03-05.
- Clay Koplin estimates that 20 to 25 percent of Cordova's hydropower goes unused each year. [National Laboratory of the Rockies](https://www.nlr.gov/news/detail/program/2026/in-alaska-a-data-center-inside-a-power-plant-inside-a-microgrid), primary document, 2026-03-05.
- Clay Koplin said the server was literally 20 feet from the generators. [National Laboratory of the Rockies](https://www.nlr.gov/news/detail/program/2026/in-alaska-a-data-center-inside-a-power-plant-inside-a-microgrid), primary document, 2026-03-05.
- Clay Koplin is chief executive officer of Cordova Electric Cooperative. [National Laboratory of the Rockies](https://www.nlr.gov/news/detail/program/2026/in-alaska-a-data-center-inside-a-power-plant-inside-a-microgrid), primary document, 2026-03-05.
- The Department of Energy and Cordova incrementally developed a smart microgrid from 2017 to 2023. [National Laboratory of the Rockies](https://www.nlr.gov/news/detail/program/2026/in-alaska-a-data-center-inside-a-power-plant-inside-a-microgrid), primary document, 2026-03-05.
- A digital twin of Cordova's microgrid was built by the National Laboratory of the Rockies alongside Idaho National Laboratory, Pacific Northwest National Laboratory and Sandia National Laboratories. [National Laboratory of the Rockies](https://www.nlr.gov/news/detail/program/2026/in-alaska-a-data-center-inside-a-power-plant-inside-a-microgrid), primary document, 2026-03-05.
- Greensparc is the edge data center provider that installed the computing on the floor of the Cordova power station. [National Laboratory of the Rockies](https://www.nlr.gov/news/detail/program/2026/in-alaska-a-data-center-inside-a-power-plant-inside-a-microgrid), primary document, 2026-03-05.
- Cordova Electric Cooperative serves 1,566 customers. [Cordova Electric Cooperative](https://www.cordovaelectric.com/about/), primary document, 2026-08-12.
- Cordova Electric Cooperative has a generating capacity of 18 megawatts. [Cordova Electric Cooperative](https://www.cordovaelectric.com/about/), primary document, 2026-08-12.
- Cordova is not connected to the State Highway System and Cordova Electric Cooperative is not connected by transmission line to other communities. [Cordova Electric Cooperative](https://www.cordovaelectric.com/about/), primary document, 2026-08-12.
- The Department of Energy renamed the National Renewable Energy Laboratory the National Laboratory of the Rockies effective December 1st, 2025. [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/articles/energy-department-renames-nrel-national-lab-rockies), primary document, 2025-12-01.
- Alaska DNR has preliminarily decided to authorize a 50 year lease of 715.4 acres to STAK Energy Corporation about 26 miles south of Deadhorse. [Alaska Department of Natural Resources Division of Oil and Gas](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224224), primary document, 2026-06-17.
- The public comment period on the STAK Energy lease closed at 4:30 p.m. Alaska Daylight Time on July 17th, 2026. [Alaska Department of Natural Resources Division of Oil and Gas](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224224), primary document, 2026-06-17.
- The STAK Energy lease notice is a preliminary decision and no final finding and decision has been published. [Alaska Department of Natural Resources Division of Oil and Gas](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224224), primary document, 2026-06-17.
- The state notice describes the STAK Energy campus as a commercial natural gas powered energy facility with on site natural gas power generation infrastructure, so its electricity would be generated for itself rather than drawn from an existing Alaska utility grid. [Alaska Department of Natural Resources Division of Oil and Gas](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224224), primary document, 2026-06-17.
- Exactly one of the 278 rows on the Department of Energy's Genesis Mission awards list is an Alaska institution, the University of Alaska Fairbanks project AURORA-AI led by Richard Wies. [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2026-07/GM-RFA-Awards-List.pdf), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- Cordova has about 2,600 residents. [National Laboratory of the Rockies](https://www.nlr.gov/news/detail/program/2026/in-alaska-a-data-center-inside-a-power-plant-inside-a-microgrid), report, 2026-03-05.

# The Ladder Stops at Fifth Grade

> 15 minutes a day. That is the routine technology cap a Kenai Peninsula Borough School District draft would set for kindergarten.

Published 2026-08-09 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-08-09/

## The story

A five year old gets a number. A senior gets an adjective.

One draft. Two kinds of answer.

The AI draft draws no grade line.

The district calls this a new administrative regulation brought forward in relation to the inclusion of AI. Two competing drafts were posted. The committee postponed it on July 6th.

They disagree about the line, not the verb.

One room. Two meetings. No posted outcome.

Seven documents. None adopted on the posted record.

The state framework is a benchmark, not a floor.

Alaska's Strategic Framework, Artificial Intelligence for K-12, sets seven guiding principles. It is the document the district group compared its own material against last fall. No published source makes it binding on the district.

The drafts are still drafts. The dates aren't.

Save this. None of it is settled.

## What we verified

- The KPBSD Policy Review Committee meeting of August 3, 2026 was scheduled to start at 10:00 AM. [KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://egov.kpbsd.org/meetings/666), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The August 3rd Policy Review Committee meeting was held in the Betty J. Glick Assembly Chambers in Soldotna. [KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://egov.kpbsd.org/meetings/666), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The August 3rd Policy Review Committee agenda carried eight numbered policy or exhibit documents across four review sections. [KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- AR 5131.9 Academic Honesty appeared on the August 3rd committee agenda under the heading Policy Review-Ongoing. [KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The district describes AR 5131.9 Academic Honesty as a new administrative regulation brought forward in relation to the inclusion of AI. [KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666?item=10054), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- Two competing drafts of AR 5131.9 were posted to the August 3rd agenda item, one from Administration and one from board member VanBuskirk. [KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666?item=10054), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The Policy Review Committee postponed AR 5131.9 at its July 6, 2026 meeting and carried it to the next committee meeting. [KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://egov.kpbsd.org/meetings/661/minutes), primary document, 2026-07-06.
- The Administration draft of AR 5131.9 opens by tying academic honesty directly to artificial intelligence. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 5131.9 draft](https://egov.kpbsd.org/api/v1/documents/6187/download), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The AR 5131.9 draft makes misuse of AI tools a violation of academic honesty subject to discipline under BP 5144. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 5131.9 draft](https://egov.kpbsd.org/api/v1/documents/6187/download), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The AR 5131.9 draft reserves the district's right to monitor and review student use of AI tools. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 5131.9 draft](https://egov.kpbsd.org/api/v1/documents/6187/download), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The posted drafts of AR 5131.9 appear to draw no grade line, applying the same AI rule to every student. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 5131.9 draft](https://egov.kpbsd.org/api/v1/documents/6187/download), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The VanBuskirk draft of AR 5131.9 permits AI as an instructional tool when it supports the objectives of the assignment. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 5131.9 VanBuskirk draft](https://egov.kpbsd.org/api/v1/documents/6188/download), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The VanBuskirk draft of AR 5131.9 states that AI is meant to enhance learning and not to replace student thinking. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 5131.9 VanBuskirk draft](https://egov.kpbsd.org/api/v1/documents/6188/download), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- BP 6161.5 High-Quality Instruction and Purposeful Use of Technology came to the August 3rd committee as a brand new policy. [KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666?item=10087), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- AR 6161.5 was presented as the administrative regulation accompanying the newly drafted BP 6161.5. [KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666?item=10088), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- BP 6161.5 states that technology is one instructional tool among many and is not the instructional program. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, BP 6161.5 draft](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666?item=10087), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- BP 6161.5 says the board expects technology to support rather than replace relationships and instruction. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, BP 6161.5 draft](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666?item=10087), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- AR 6161.5 caps routine instructional technology use at 15 minutes a day in kindergarten and first grade. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 6161.5 draft](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666?item=10088), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- AR 6161.5 caps routine instructional technology use at 20 minutes a day in second grade. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 6161.5 draft](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666?item=10088), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- AR 6161.5 caps routine instructional technology use at 60 minutes a day in third grade. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 6161.5 draft](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666?item=10088), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- AR 6161.5 caps routine instructional technology use at 90 minutes a day in fourth and fifth grade. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 6161.5 draft](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666?item=10088), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- AR 6161.5 sets no routine daily technology limit for secondary schools. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 6161.5 draft](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666?item=10088), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- AR 6161.5 addresses grades 6 through 12 with a qualitative standard instead of a minute figure. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 6161.5 draft](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666?item=10088), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- AR 6161.5 says technology should not serve as the default instructional method where hands on learning offers greater educational value. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 6161.5 draft](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666?item=10088), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- AR 6161.5 excludes assessments, distance education and intervention services from the routine use it limits. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 6161.5 draft](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666?item=10088), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The screen time drafts BP 6161.5 and AR 6161.5 do not mention artificial intelligence. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, BP 6161.5 and AR 6161.5 drafts](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666?item=10088), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The full board's regular business meeting on the evening of August 3rd took a first reading of BP 5131.9 Academic Honesty on its consent agenda. [KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/667), primary document, 2026-08-03.

- The district describes the AR 5125 Student Records revisions as recommended by Administration regarding AI-related policy shifts. [KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/667?item=10051), primary document, 2026-08-03.

- The district describes the BP 5131.9 revisions as recommended by Administration regarding AI-related policy shifts. [KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/667?item=10053), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The KPBSD board's regular business meeting on August 3rd began at 6:00 PM, eight hours after the policy committee convened. [KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://egov.kpbsd.org/meetings/667), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The next regular KPBSD board meeting after August 3rd is scheduled for September 14, 2026. [KPBSD E-Governance, Board Meeting and Work Sessions Dates 2026-2027](https://egov.kpbsd.org/library/items/25), primary document, 2026-08-09.
- KPBSD reports an enrollment of about 8,300 students. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://www.kpbsd.org/), primary document, 2026-08-09.
- KPBSD operates 39 schools. [Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://www.kpbsd.org/), primary document, 2026-08-09.

- MagicSchool markets itself on its homepage as safe district aligned AI for schools. [MagicSchool AI](https://www.magicschool.ai/), primary document, 2026-08-09.
- Alaska's state AI guidance for schools is titled Alaska's Strategic Framework, Artificial Intelligence for K-12, issued by the Department of Education and Early Development. [Alaska Department of Education and Early Development](https://education.alaska.gov/artificial-intelligence), primary document, 2026-08-09.
- The Alaska DEED AI framework is built on seven guiding principles beginning with human-centered use. [Alaska Department of Education and Early Development](https://education.alaska.gov/artificial-intelligence), primary document, 2026-08-09.
- The Alaska DEED AI framework's cultural responsiveness principle asks that AI tools affirm rather than diminish Alaska's diverse cultures. [Alaska Department of Education and Early Development](https://education.alaska.gov/artificial-intelligence), primary document, 2026-08-09.
- The July 6th committee record shows the board asked for a demonstration or training on AI before settling the policies. [KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://egov.kpbsd.org/meetings/661/minutes), primary document, 2026-07-06.
- No minutes are posted for either of the August 3rd meetings, so the outcome of that day is not on the public record. [KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://egov.kpbsd.org/meetings/666/minutes), primary document, 2026-08-09.
- The July 6th committee minutes are posted and are marked approved on August 3, 2026, the same day whose own minutes are not posted. [KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District](https://egov.kpbsd.org/meetings/661/minutes), primary document, 2026-07-06.

- KBBI reported in July that district administrators hope to implement the new AI policies by the beginning of the new school year. [KBBI AM 890](https://www.kbbi.org/2026-07-08/proposed-school-district-ai-policies-target-academic-honesty-student-privacy), report, 2026-07-08.
- Kenai High School assistant principal Will Chervenak said the technology policy defines the district's ethos and its view of high quality instruction. [KDLL 91.9 FM](https://www.kdll.org/local-news/2026-08-03/school-board-considers-classroom-screen-time-limits), report, 2026-08-03.
- KDLL reported that August 3rd was the first time board members saw the pair of screen time proposals. [KDLL 91.9 FM](https://www.kdll.org/local-news/2026-08-03/school-board-considers-classroom-screen-time-limits), report, 2026-08-03.

# Redoubt Weir. Lit To Install, Dark To Run

> Solar panels and a Starlink system on a lagoon float run an AI salmon counter at Redoubt Lake, 15 miles by boat from Sitka.

Published 2026-08-08 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-08-08/

## The story

"The system is not broken. That's the problem."

One camera. One chute. One fish at a time.

This number sets a household's legal limit.

The power and the uplink float on top.

$200,000 paid to install it. Once.

Grant money lights damage.

What this weir has actually measured.

Nobody has published a count of the counter.

A working instrument with no line item.

## What we verified

- The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service listed a fiscal year 2024 Tribal Wildlife Grant to the Sitka Tribe of Alaska titled "Artificial Intelligence for Subsistence Salmon Monitoring and Management". [U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service](https://www.fws.gov/press-release/2024-10/service-awards-more-64-million-tribal-wildlife-grants-advance-shared), primary document, 2024-10-16.
- The Redoubt Lake weir was installed on June 14th, 2026 for the 2026 season. [Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Sport Fish](https://www.adfg.alaska.gov/sf/EONR/index.cfm?ADFG=region.NR&Year=2026&NRID=4070), primary document, 2026-06-30.
- The weir had counted 7,791 sockeye salmon by June 29th, 2026. [Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Sport Fish](https://www.adfg.alaska.gov/sf/EONR/index.cfm?ADFG=region.NR&Year=2026&NRID=4070), primary document, 2026-06-30.
- The department said projected escapement for the 2026 Redoubt season exceeds 40,000 sockeye salmon. [Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Sport Fish](https://www.adfg.alaska.gov/sf/EONR/index.cfm?ADFG=region.NR&Year=2026&NRID=4070), primary document, 2026-06-30.
- Salmon Vision reports a mean average precision of 80.2 percent for its detection model. [Salmon Vision Collaborative](https://salmonvision.org/), primary document, 2026-08-08.
- Salmon Vision reports detecting 6 salmon species among 17 total species. [Salmon Vision Collaborative](https://salmonvision.org/), primary document, 2026-08-08.
- Salmon Vision reports its models were trained on over 5 million annotated frames. [Salmon Vision Collaborative](https://salmonvision.org/), primary document, 2026-08-08.
- Salmon Vision publishes its model code under an MIT open research license and its data and annotations under a Creative Commons BY-NC-SA 4.0 license. [Salmon Vision Collaborative](https://salmonvision.org/about/), primary document, 2026-08-08.
- Salmon Vision describes itself as a collaborative effort by the Pacific Salmon Foundation, Wild Salmon Center, Simon Fraser University computing sciences and Lumax Ecological Analytics. [Salmon Vision Collaborative](https://salmonvision.org/about/), primary document, 2026-08-08.
- Salmon Vision lists the Sitka Tribe of Alaska among its partners, alongside the Alaska Department of Fish and Game and Fisheries and Oceans Canada. [Salmon Vision Collaborative](https://salmonvision.org/), primary document, 2026-08-08.
- That Tribal Wildlife Grant to the Sitka Tribe of Alaska was $200,000. [U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service](https://www.fws.gov/press-release/2024-10/service-awards-more-64-million-tribal-wildlife-grants-advance-shared), primary document, 2024-10-16.
- The Service described the award as paying to install artificial intelligence enabled video producing automated real time counts of Redoubt Lake sockeye salmon and reducing real time monitoring costs. [U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service](https://www.fws.gov/press-release/2024-10/service-awards-more-64-million-tribal-wildlife-grants-advance-shared), primary document, 2024-10-16.
- The Service's Alaska release said the Sitka Tribe of Alaska would partner with the Wild Salmon Center and the U.S. Forest Service to install the AI enabled video chutes. [U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service](https://www.fws.gov/press-release/2024-10/us-fish-wildlife-service-awards-more-13-million-tribal-wildlife-grants-alaska), primary document, 2024-10-17.
- The Service said it was awarding more than $1.3 million in Tribal Wildlife Grants to federally recognized Tribes in Alaska in that round. [U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service](https://www.fws.gov/press-release/2024-10/us-fish-wildlife-service-awards-more-13-million-tribal-wildlife-grants-alaska), primary document, 2024-10-17.
- The Alaska Department of Fish and Game raised the annual subsistence limit for Redoubt Bay and Lake sockeye salmon to 100 fish per individual or household. [Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Sport Fish](https://www.adfg.alaska.gov/sf/EONR/index.cfm?ADFG=region.NR&Year=2026&NRID=4070), primary document, 2026-06-30.
- The same emergency order set the Redoubt subsistence possession limit at 25 sockeye salmon per individual or household. [Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Sport Fish](https://www.adfg.alaska.gov/sf/EONR/index.cfm?ADFG=region.NR&Year=2026&NRID=4070), primary document, 2026-06-30.
- The same order set the Redoubt sport bag and possession limit at 6 sockeye salmon. [Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Sport Fish](https://www.adfg.alaska.gov/sf/EONR/index.cfm?ADFG=region.NR&Year=2026&NRID=4070), primary document, 2026-06-30.
- The liberalized Redoubt limits took effect at 12:01 a.m. on July 1st, 2026. [Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Sport Fish](https://www.adfg.alaska.gov/sf/EONR/index.cfm?ADFG=region.NR&Year=2026&NRID=4070), primary document, 2026-06-30.
- Jeff Feldpausch, resource protection director for the Sitka Tribe of Alaska, said there is no funding for the weir right now. [KCAW Raven Radio, reporting by Hope McKenney](https://www.kcaw.org/2026/08/05/theres-no-funding-for-the-weir-right-now-sitka-tribe-of-alaska-introduces-ai-monitoring-at-redoubt/), report, 2026-08-05.
- Feldpausch said the Tribe looked high and low for grant sources and all of them deal with systems that need remediation. [KCAW Raven Radio, reporting by Hope McKenney](https://www.kcaw.org/2026/08/05/theres-no-funding-for-the-weir-right-now-sitka-tribe-of-alaska-introduces-ai-monitoring-at-redoubt/), report, 2026-08-05.
- Feldpausch said there is lots of money to fix and monitor broken systems but no regular funding for a system that is not broken. [KCAW Raven Radio, reporting by Hope McKenney](https://www.kcaw.org/2026/08/05/theres-no-funding-for-the-weir-right-now-sitka-tribe-of-alaska-introduces-ai-monitoring-at-redoubt/), report, 2026-08-05.
- Feldpausch said the computer has learned to count sockeye and the program has reached about a 95 percent confidence interval on counting sockeye through the system. [KCAW Raven Radio, reporting by Hope McKenney](https://www.kcaw.org/2026/08/05/theres-no-funding-for-the-weir-right-now-sitka-tribe-of-alaska-introduces-ai-monitoring-at-redoubt/), report, 2026-08-05.
- Feldpausch said a commercial fishery is now taking place at Redoubt that would not happen if the weir were not in place. [KCAW Raven Radio, reporting by Hope McKenney](https://www.kcaw.org/2026/08/05/theres-no-funding-for-the-weir-right-now-sitka-tribe-of-alaska-introduces-ai-monitoring-at-redoubt/), report, 2026-08-05.
- Feldpausch said harvesters can now take up to 100 sockeye a year, up from 50, and that this would not have happened without the weir. [KCAW Raven Radio, reporting by Hope McKenney](https://www.kcaw.org/2026/08/05/theres-no-funding-for-the-weir-right-now-sitka-tribe-of-alaska-introduces-ai-monitoring-at-redoubt/), report, 2026-08-05.
- Feldpausch said conflicts between people and bears are emerging because bears cannot fish the weir pool away from where people fish in the saltwater. [KCAW Raven Radio, reporting by Hope McKenney](https://www.kcaw.org/2026/08/05/theres-no-funding-for-the-weir-right-now-sitka-tribe-of-alaska-introduces-ai-monitoring-at-redoubt/), report, 2026-08-05.
- Feldpausch said runs at Redoubt were significantly depressed in the early 1980s with around 800 sockeye returning. [KCAW Raven Radio, reporting by Hope McKenney](https://www.kcaw.org/2026/08/05/theres-no-funding-for-the-weir-right-now-sitka-tribe-of-alaska-introduces-ai-monitoring-at-redoubt/), report, 2026-08-05.
- KCAW described the Redoubt setup as a white polyethylene plastic chute with a video camera on the side, with a float in the lagoon carrying battery packs, solar panels and a Starlink system. [KCAW Raven Radio, reporting by Hope McKenney](https://www.kcaw.org/2026/08/05/theres-no-funding-for-the-weir-right-now-sitka-tribe-of-alaska-introduces-ai-monitoring-at-redoubt/), report, 2026-08-05.
- KCAW reported that data from the Redoubt system is uploaded online immediately and is accessible from the Tribe's office in Sitka. [KCAW Raven Radio, reporting by Hope McKenney](https://www.kcaw.org/2026/08/05/theres-no-funding-for-the-weir-right-now-sitka-tribe-of-alaska-introduces-ai-monitoring-at-redoubt/), report, 2026-08-05.
- Redoubt Falls is a 15 mile boat ride from downtown Sitka. [KCAW Raven Radio, reporting by Hope McKenney](https://www.kcaw.org/2026/08/05/theres-no-funding-for-the-weir-right-now-sitka-tribe-of-alaska-introduces-ai-monitoring-at-redoubt/), report, 2026-08-05.
- KCAW identified the Redoubt counting system as coming from the British Columbia based company SalmonVision. [KCAW Raven Radio, reporting by Hope McKenney](https://www.kcaw.org/2026/08/05/theres-no-funding-for-the-weir-right-now-sitka-tribe-of-alaska-introduces-ai-monitoring-at-redoubt/), report, 2026-08-05.
- Technicians counted nearly 229,000 sockeye entering Redoubt Lake while operating the weir from mid June to late July of 2025. [Ketchikan Daily News, reprinting Anna Laffrey of the Daily Sitka Sentinel](https://www.ketchikandailynews.com/news/waterfront/redoubt-lake-sockeye-salmon-boom-spurs-study/article_0152260b-191c-486b-b905-4690f2b77baa.html), report, 2025-10-25.
- Redoubt weir counts were 153,406 fish in 2023 and 210,253 in 2024 according to U.S. Forest Service reports. [Ketchikan Daily News, reprinting Anna Laffrey of the Daily Sitka Sentinel](https://www.ketchikandailynews.com/news/waterfront/redoubt-lake-sockeye-salmon-boom-spurs-study/article_0152260b-191c-486b-b905-4690f2b77baa.html), report, 2025-10-25.
- A researcher found that about 35 percent of all subsistence sockeye harvest in Southeast Alaska happens at Redoubt, based on unpublished Forest Service and Fish and Game data. [Ketchikan Daily News, reprinting Anna Laffrey of the Daily Sitka Sentinel](https://www.ketchikandailynews.com/news/waterfront/redoubt-lake-sockeye-salmon-boom-spurs-study/article_0152260b-191c-486b-b905-4690f2b77baa.html), report, 2025-10-25.
- The AI camera system at Redoubt captured 2,600 video clips in two and a half weeks during 2025. [Ketchikan Daily News, reprinting Anna Laffrey of the Daily Sitka Sentinel](https://www.ketchikandailynews.com/news/waterfront/redoubt-lake-sockeye-salmon-boom-spurs-study/article_0152260b-191c-486b-b905-4690f2b77baa.html), report, 2025-10-25.
- Sitka Tribe technicians installed the AI equipment at Redoubt in August 2025 and it was reported as the first in-stream artificial intelligence fish count in Alaska. [Ketchikan Daily News, reprinting Anna Laffrey of the Daily Sitka Sentinel](https://www.ketchikandailynews.com/news/waterfront/redoubt-lake-sockeye-salmon-boom-spurs-study/article_0152260b-191c-486b-b905-4690f2b77baa.html), report, 2025-10-25.
- Seiners caught about 130,000 sockeye at Redoubt in 2025, the largest commercial harvest there since at least 1985. [Ketchikan Daily News, reprinting Anna Laffrey of the Daily Sitka Sentinel](https://www.ketchikandailynews.com/news/waterfront/redoubt-lake-sockeye-salmon-boom-spurs-study/article_0152260b-191c-486b-b905-4690f2b77baa.html), report, 2025-10-25.
- The U.S. Forest Service and the Sitka Tribe of Alaska issued a joint bear warning for Redoubt Falls on July 30th, 2026, saying several brown bears including two sows with cubs were frequenting the weir. # More Than 600 Were Citizens. About 1,900 Never Answered

> Alaska's elections director told lawmakers more than 600 citizens came off the active voter list and she won't restore them herself.

Published 2026-08-07 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-08-07/

## What we verified

- The Alaska Division of Elections posted a notice titled Division of Elections responds to lawmakers' inquiry on August 6th, 2026. [Alaska Division of Elections](https://www.elections.alaska.gov/division-of-elections-responds-to-lawmakers-inquiry/), primary document, 2026-08-06.
- The Alaska Division of Elections lists the 2026 primary election as August 18, 2026 and the general election as November 3, 2026. [Alaska Division of Elections](https://www.elections.alaska.gov/election-information/), primary document, 2026-08-07.
- The Division of Elections says absentee in person and early voting locations are open for voting starting 15 days prior to and through Election Day. [Alaska Division of Elections](https://www.elections.alaska.gov/voter-information/absentee-and-early-voting/), primary document, 2026-08-07.
- The deadline to request an absentee ballot by mail for the 2026 primary is August 8th, 2026. [Alaska Division of Elections](https://www.elections.alaska.gov/voter-information/absentee-and-early-voting/), primary document, 2026-08-07.
- More than 600 U.S. citizens were mistakenly flagged as possible noncitizens and removed from Alaska's list of active voters, according to the Division of Elections director's letter to lawmakers. [Alaska Beacon (James Brooks)](https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/), report, 2026-08-06.
- The Beacon reported that 3,058 people were removed from Alaska's active voter list after the Division of Elections compared its citizenship data against Division of Motor Vehicles records. [Alaska Beacon (James Brooks)](https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/), report, 2026-08-06.
- Alaska Public Media reported on July 23rd, 2026 that a Division of Elections spokesman gave the specific figure of 3,048. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/2026-07-23/state-removes-3-500-alaskans-from-voter-rolls-based-in-part-on-old-data), report, 2026-07-23.
- Elections Director Carol Beecher wrote that approximately 685 voters have contacted the Division and stated they are citizens despite the inconsistency with the DMV's records. [Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), quoting the Beecher letter](https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/), report, 2026-08-06.
- Beecher wrote that more than 100 people have reported they are not citizens and requested that their voter registration be cancelled. [Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), quoting the Beecher letter](https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/), report, 2026-08-06.
- About 350 of the letters the Division of Elections sent to affected Alaskans were returned as undeliverable. [Alaska Beacon (James Brooks)](https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/), report, 2026-08-06.
- About 1,900 affected Alaskans have not responded at all to the Division's letter. [Alaska Beacon (James Brooks)](https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/), report, 2026-08-06.
- In 2024 the DMV and the Division of Elections compared just 2,000 records. [Alaska Beacon (James Brooks)](https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/), report, 2026-08-06.
- More than 580,000 records were compared this year, a volume the DMV called non-routine. [Alaska Beacon (James Brooks)](https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/), report, 2026-08-06.
- Beecher wrote that the Division has paused additional DMV comparisons while it evaluates this initial effort and incorporates lessons learned. [Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), quoting the Beecher letter](https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/), report, 2026-08-06.
- Beecher said she will not unilaterally return affected Alaskans to the voter rolls and that the division will instead send out another notice to affected voters. [Alaska Beacon (James Brooks)](https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/), report, 2026-08-06.
- Someone removed from the voter list may still cast a vote this year but will not appear on their precinct register and must provide additional identity information to cast a questioned ballot. [Alaska Beacon (James Brooks)](https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/), report, 2026-08-06.
- A joint statement from the Division of Motor Vehicles and the Division of Elections said Elections most recently asked DMV to compare lists in March 2026, producing the letters that were recently sent. [Alaska's News Source, quoting the joint DMV and Division of Elections statement](https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/07/30/lawmakers-say-elections-division-illegally-deactivated-registration-thousands-voters-urges-director-reverse-decision/), report, 2026-07-29.
- Beecher said the Division of Elections sent a letter to about 3,500 Alaskans. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/2026-07-23/state-removes-3-500-alaskans-from-voter-rolls-based-in-part-on-old-data), report, 2026-07-23.
- A bipartisan group of 23 legislators wrote to Elections Director Carol Beecher asking that all names be put back on the active voters list unless ineligibility has been established. [KMXT / Alaska Public Media (Liz Ruskin)](https://www.kmxt.org/alaska-statewide-news/2026-07-30/23-alaska-legislators-ask-state-to-restore-voters-wrongfully-removed-from-the-rolls), report, 2026-07-30.
- KMXT reported that Beecher told legislators voters could get back on the voter list by contacting the division and affirming that they are citizens. [KMXT / Alaska Public Media (Liz Ruskin)](https://www.kmxt.org/alaska-statewide-news/2026-07-30/23-alaska-legislators-ask-state-to-restore-voters-wrongfully-removed-from-the-rolls), report, 2026-07-30.
- Public Citizen's election deepfake legislation tracker lists Alaska Senate Bill 64 with its election deepfake provision removed, and does not list Alaska among enacted states. [Public Citizen](https://www.citizen.org/article/tracker-legislation-on-deepfakes-in-elections/), report, 2026-08-07.
- The Alaska Legislature passed a bipartisan elections bill, Senate Bill 64, that would have improved voter roll list maintenance, and Gov. Mike Dunleavy vetoed it before an override attempt failed. [Alaska Beacon (James Brooks)](https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/), report, 2026-08-06.
- The Division of Elections disclosed a list last year which showed 70 noncitizens either voted or attempted to vote in elections over the past decade. [Alaska Beacon (James Brooks)](https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/), report, 2026-08-06.
- Beecher dismissed an Anchorage temporary poll worker after she raised concerns about how poll workers were instructed to handle voters flagged as possible noncitizens. [Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), quoting an email from Carol Beecher](https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/), report, 2026-08-06.

Slides and the deck PDF are linked from the canonical page.

# The Land Is On Offer. The Power Is Not.

> April 10th, the Air Force offered about 4,700 acres for AI data centers. August 4th, Alaska defended about 19,950 more.

Published 2026-08-06 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-08-06/

## The story

ABOUT 4,700 ACRES ON OFFER.

THE POWER IS NOT.

The sites have "insufficient power" for a data center

APPROXIMATELY 19,950 ACRES NORTH OF HOUSTON.

"It just comes down to the fact that nobody has the gas right now that they're willing to sell."

Four prices. One unit. Different things.

About 4 billion cubic feet. The target is 7.

Thirty minutes at a time, in the worst case.

"The clock is ticking very loudly right now."

Comment on the DNR preliminary decision by August 19th.

## What we verified

- AIDEA deputy director Brandon Brefczynski wrote that there is no committed data center tenant, industrial developer, site plan, power source, cooling system, water supply plan or construction schedule. [Anchorage Daily News opinion, signed by AIDEA deputy director Brandon Brefczynski](https://www.adn.com/opinions/2026/08/04/opinion-the-best-time-to-shape-mat-su-development-is-before-it-begins/), primary document, 2026-08-04.
- The Alaska Department of Natural Resources preliminary decision concerns approximately 19,950 acres north of Houston. [Anchorage Daily News opinion, signed by AIDEA deputy director Brandon Brefczynski](https://www.adn.com/opinions/2026/08/04/opinion-the-best-time-to-shape-mat-su-development-is-before-it-begins/), primary document, 2026-08-04.
- The DNR preliminary decision remains open for public comment through August 19th, after which DNR will decide whether and under what conditions to proceed. [Anchorage Daily News opinion, signed by AIDEA deputy director Brandon Brefczynski](https://www.adn.com/opinions/2026/08/04/opinion-the-best-time-to-shape-mat-su-development-is-before-it-begins/), primary document, 2026-08-04.
- AIDEA says it has declared approximately 495 million dollars in dividends to the state, including the dividend declared for fiscal year 2026. [Anchorage Daily News opinion, signed by AIDEA deputy director Brandon Brefczynski](https://www.adn.com/opinions/2026/08/04/opinion-the-best-time-to-shape-mat-su-development-is-before-it-begins/), primary document, 2026-08-04.
- Fed Governor Lisa D. Cook said in Anchorage that the most dire predictions about AI job losses have not materialized and that she still sees the development as a significant risk that has not grown over the past year. [Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/cook20260805a.htm), primary document, 2026-08-05.
- Overall business investment rose at a 10 percent annual rate in the first half of the year, Fed Governor Lisa D. Cook said. [Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/cook20260805a.htm), primary document, 2026-08-05.
- Alaska's unemployment rate is 4.4 percent according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, as cited by Fed Governor Lisa D. Cook in Anchorage. [Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/cook20260805a.htm), primary document, 2026-08-05.
- Enstar has already turned away new, large-scale customers in order to focus on supplying existing ratepayers, Alaska Public Media reported, citing president and CEO John Sims. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/economy/energy/2026-07-28/southcentral-alaska-gas-utility-says-bills-likely-to-rise-amid-supply-shortage), report, 2026-07-28.

- Enstar's standard contract price for Hilcorp gas is 8.78 dollars per thousand cubic feet. [Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/economy/energy/2026-07-28/as-winter-approaches-southcentral-alaska-utilities-are-worried-about-running-short-of-gas), report, 2026-07-28.
- Enstar offered new producers a premium of 17.50 dollars per thousand cubic feet and its president said it has not encouraged companies to drill more. [Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/economy/energy/2026-07-28/as-winter-approaches-southcentral-alaska-utilities-are-worried-about-running-short-of-gas), report, 2026-07-28.
- Enstar president John Sims said nobody has the gas right now that they are willing to sell. [Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/economy/energy/2026-07-28/as-winter-approaches-southcentral-alaska-utilities-are-worried-about-running-short-of-gas), report, 2026-07-28.

- Gov. Mike Dunleavy rejected a conference committee bill and called a third Alaska LNG special session beginning July 27th. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/alaska-legislature/2026-07-16/dunleavy-rejecting-corporate-tax-change-calls-third-alaska-lng-special-session), report, 2026-07-16.
- The Alaska Senate passed the LNG tax measure 11 to 8 on July 16th and the House vote ended in a 19 to 19 tie. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/alaska-legislature/2026-07-16/dunleavy-rejecting-corporate-tax-change-calls-third-alaska-lng-special-session), report, 2026-07-16.
- The Alaska LNG project is expected to cost as much as 54.5 billion dollars. [Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/alaska-legislature/2026-07-20/hilcorp-killed-alaska-lng-bill-some-legislators-say-but-governor-calls-the-claim-bulls-t), report, 2026-07-20.
- The rejected LNG bill would have required the state and local governments to forgo more than 10 billion dollars in revenue over 30 years. [Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/alaska-legislature/2026-07-20/hilcorp-killed-alaska-lng-bill-some-legislators-say-but-governor-calls-the-claim-bulls-t), report, 2026-07-20.
- House Speaker Bryce Edgmon said the clock is ticking very loudly and that if it is not done this special session he does not know that there will be another opportunity this year. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/alaska-legislature/2026-07-27/lawmakers-say-third-alaska-lng-session-is-dunleavys-last-chance-to-make-a-deal), report, 2026-07-27.
- The Air Force solicitation AFCEC-26-R-0006 sought AI data center development at Joint Base Elmendorf Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station, with responses due June 29th, 2026. [HigherGov, aggregating the federal solicitation](https://www.highergov.com/contract-opportunity/rflp-artificial-intelligence-ai-data-center-deve-afcec-26-r-0006-o-db695/), report, 2026-04-10.
- The Air Force offered five sites for lease at Joint Base Elmendorf Richardson ranging from about 60 acres to nearly 200 acres. [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/alaska-news/military/2026/05/05/the-military-wants-to-host-data-centers-in-alaska-raising-questions-about-whether-theres-enough-gas-to-power-them/), report, 2026-05-05.
- The Air Force solicitation says the JBER sites have insufficient power for a data center and will require a new connection to Chugach Electric Association in Anchorage. [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/alaska-news/military/2026/05/05/the-military-wants-to-host-data-centers-in-alaska-raising-questions-about-whether-theres-enough-gas-to-power-them/), report, 2026-05-05.
- Chugach Electric's gas supply contract with Hilcorp Alaska, its primary supplier, is set to end in 2028. [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/alaska-news/military/2026/05/05/the-military-wants-to-host-data-centers-in-alaska-raising-questions-about-whether-theres-enough-gas-to-power-them/), report, 2026-05-05.
- The Air Force lease offer covers about 4,700 acres across 12 identified parcels at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station. [ExecutiveGov](https://www.executivegov.com/articles/air-force-ai-data-centers-alaska), report, 2026-04-13.

## What we verified

- The ANA final issuance appears in Federal Register Volume 91, Number 143, published Tuesday, July 28, 2026. [Federal Register (Office of the Federal Register)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/07/28/2026-15150.txt), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- The document begins at Federal Register page 47241 and runs through page 47243. [GovInfo (U.S. Government Publishing Office)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-07-28/html/2026-15150.htm), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- The issuance stands up three FY 2026 notices of funding opportunity, named EAGLE, the AI3 Action Institute and NCNTTA. [Administration for Native Americans, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/07/28/2026-15150.txt), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- The agency's own document records that multiple commenters objected to replacing SEDS-AK with EAGLE and warned Alaska Tribes could face new barriers. [Administration for Native Americans, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/07/28/2026-15150.txt), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- ANA responded that Alaska Native communities remain eligible across EAGLE project areas including IDEAS. [Administration for Native Americans, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/07/28/2026-15150.txt), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- ANA states that the EAGLE IDEAS project area carries forward the spirit of Alaskan self-determination. [Administration for Native Americans, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/07/28/2026-15150.txt), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- ANA also pledged to continue considering the distinct circumstances and needs of Alaska Native communities in future programming. [Administration for Native Americans, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/07/28/2026-15150.txt), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- IDEAS stands for Indigenous Designs to Empower and Advance Self-Determination. [Grants.gov, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://simpler.grants.gov/opportunity/bb965470-bd8d-4529-b30b-39efe6f81147), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- EAGLE has five project areas. [Grants.gov, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://simpler.grants.gov/opportunity/bb965470-bd8d-4529-b30b-39efe6f81147), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- The EAGLE opportunity number is HHS-2026-ACF-ANA-NEG-0120. [Grants.gov, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://simpler.grants.gov/opportunity/bb965470-bd8d-4529-b30b-39efe6f81147), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- EAGLE was posted on July 28, 2026 and closes on August 27, 2026. [Grants.gov, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://simpler.grants.gov/opportunity/bb965470-bd8d-4529-b30b-39efe6f81147), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- EAGLE has total program funding of $24,000,000. [Grants.gov, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://simpler.grants.gov/opportunity/bb965470-bd8d-4529-b30b-39efe6f81147), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- EAGLE expects to make 31 awards ranging from $300,000 to $1,000,000. [Grants.gov, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://simpler.grants.gov/opportunity/bb965470-bd8d-4529-b30b-39efe6f81147), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- The AI3 Action Institute opportunity number is HHS-2026-ACF-ANA-NAI-0035. [Grants.gov, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://simpler.grants.gov/opportunity/8b106d7a-a5ec-4226-b3d4-90bc8c3eade1), primary document, 2026-07-30.
- The AI3 Action Institute was posted on July 30, 2026, two days after the Federal Register issuance. [Grants.gov, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://simpler.grants.gov/opportunity/8b106d7a-a5ec-4226-b3d4-90bc8c3eade1), primary document, 2026-07-30.
- The AI3 Action Institute is a single award with an award ceiling of $3,500,000 and an award floor of $2,500,000. [Grants.gov, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://simpler.grants.gov/opportunity/8b106d7a-a5ec-4226-b3d4-90bc8c3eade1), primary document, 2026-07-30.
- Both EAGLE and the AI3 Action Institute fall under assistance listing 93.612, Native American Programs. [Grants.gov, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://simpler.grants.gov/opportunity/8b106d7a-a5ec-4226-b3d4-90bc8c3eade1), primary document, 2026-07-30.
- AI3 eligibility explicitly includes Alaska Native villages as defined in the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act and nonprofit village consortia. [Grants.gov, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://simpler.grants.gov/opportunity/8b106d7a-a5ec-4226-b3d4-90bc8c3eade1), primary document, 2026-07-30.
- Applications must be submitted no later than 11:59 pm Eastern Standard Time on the due date, in the listing's own wording. [Grants.gov, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://simpler.grants.gov/opportunity/8b106d7a-a5ec-4226-b3d4-90bc8c3eade1), primary document, 2026-07-30.
- ANA states the Institute will complement rather than replace broader social and economic development efforts and will address ethical, practical and governance considerations of emerging technologies. [Administration for Native Americans, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/07/28/2026-15150.txt), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- ANA describes the AI3 Action Institute as reducing the learning curve for hundreds of Native communities and supporting the thoughtful integration of AI across Indian Country. [Grants.gov, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://simpler.grants.gov/opportunity/8b106d7a-a5ec-4226-b3d4-90bc8c3eade1), primary document, 2026-07-30.
- A commenter told ANA that consolidating training and technical assistance into a single NCNTTA agreement equates to a reduction of more than 70 percent in regional staffing capacity. [Administration for Native Americans, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/07/28/2026-15150.txt), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- ANA corrected the commenter and said the NCNTTA funding level is 3.1 million per fiscal year rather than over three years. [GovInfo (U.S. Government Publishing Office)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-07-28/html/2026-15150.htm), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- ANA frames EAGLE as an evolution of SEDS rather than a cancellation. [GovInfo (U.S. Government Publishing Office)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-07-28/html/2026-15150.htm), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- The AI3 Action Institute closes on August 27, 2026, the same date as EAGLE. [Grants.gov, HHS Administration for Children and Families](https://simpler.grants.gov/opportunity/8b106d7a-a5ec-4226-b3d4-90bc8c3eade1), primary document, 2026-07-30.
- Tribal Business News reports the new grants replace SEDS and SEDS-Alaska, which for more than 30 years let tribes propose economic development based on local priorities. [Tribal Business News](https://tribalbusinessnews.com/sections/economic-development/15712-ana-opens-27-5m-in-new-tribal-grants-replacing-decades-old-economic-development-program), report, 2026-08-04.
- Tribal Business News reports that ANA has not announced a SEDS funding opportunity for fiscal 2026. [Tribal Business News](https://tribalbusinessnews.com/sections/economic-development/15712-ana-opens-27-5m-in-new-tribal-grants-replacing-decades-old-economic-development-program), report, 2026-08-04.
- The Alaska Federation of Natives called EAGLE a very narrowly targeted program whose funding largely does not meet the needs of Alaska's tribes. [Native News Online](https://nativenewsonline.net/currents/alaska-federation-of-natives-urges-action-ahead-of-deadline-on-key-economic-development-programs/), report, 2026-04-14.
- Tribal Business News characterizes the change as shifting federal support from tribally determined projects to administration defined priorities including greenhouses, microgrids, welding and artificial intelligence. [Tribal Business News](https://tribalbusinessnews.com/sections/economic-development/15712-ana-opens-27-5m-in-new-tribal-grants-replacing-decades-old-economic-development-program), report, 2026-08-04.

# Drawn to Scale, Except the Demand

> One column tallies 119.7 megawatts becoming 120.0. The other tallies about 4,700 acres. No unit joins them.

Published 2026-08-04 by Alaska AI. 10 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-08-04/

## What we verified

- The Alaska Energy Authority's non-capacity amendment application for the Bradley Lake Hydroelectric Project is docketed at FERC as Project No. 8221-124 and was filed on June 30, 2026. [Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, via govinfo.gov](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-08-03/html/2026-15691.htm), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- FERC published the notice soliciting comments, motions to intervene and protests in the Federal Register on August 3, 2026. [Federal Register (FERC)](https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents/2026-15691.json), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- Comments, motions to intervene and protests on the Dixon Diversion amendment are due by August 28, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time. [Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, via govinfo.gov](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-08-03/html/2026-15691.htm), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The amendment proposes a new diversion dam to divert meltwater and surface runoff coming from the Dixon Glacier into Bradley Lake. [Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, via govinfo.gov](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-08-03/html/2026-15691.htm), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The amendment would raise Bradley Lake's normal maximum operating pool elevation by approximately 16 feet through spillway modifications and raising the dam embankment. [Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, via govinfo.gov](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-08-03/html/2026-15691.htm), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The amendment would install a 0.3 megawatt micro-hydro turbine in one of the Bradley Lake Dam's fishwater release valves. [Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, via govinfo.gov](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-08-03/html/2026-15691.htm), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The project's installed capacity would rise from 119.7 megawatts to 120.0 megawatts, a gain of 0.3 megawatts. [Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, via govinfo.gov](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-08-03/html/2026-15691.htm), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- FERC's notice states the amendment would increase the project's average annual power generation by approximately 38 percent. [Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, via govinfo.gov](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-08-03/html/2026-15691.htm), primary document, 2026-08-03.
- The Alaska Energy Authority estimates the Dixon Diversion construction cost at approximately $400 million. [Alaska Energy Authority](https://www.akenergyauthority.org/What-We-Do/Railbelt-Energy/Bradley-Lake-Hydroelectric-Project/Dixon-Diversion-Project), primary document, 2026-08-04.
- The Alaska Energy Authority's schedule for the Dixon Diversion is an estimated three years of study and permitting followed by three years of construction. [Alaska Energy Authority](https://www.akenergyauthority.org/What-We-Do/Railbelt-Energy/Bradley-Lake-Hydroelectric-Project/Dixon-Diversion-Project), primary document, 2026-08-04.
- The Dixon Diversion would be located five miles southwest of Bradley Lake and approximately 27 miles northeast of Homer on the Kenai Peninsula. [Alaska Energy Authority](https://www.akenergyauthority.org/What-We-Do/Railbelt-Energy/Bradley-Lake-Hydroelectric-Project/Dixon-Diversion-Project), primary document, 2026-08-04.
- From 1995 through 2020 the Bradley Lake Hydroelectric Project averaged 392,000 megawatt hours of generation annually. [Alaska Energy Authority](https://www.akenergyauthority.org/What-We-Do/Railbelt-Energy/Bradley-Lake-Hydroelectric-Project), primary document, 2026-08-04.
- Bradley Lake provides approximately 10 percent of the total annual power used by Railbelt utilities. [Alaska Energy Authority](https://www.akenergyauthority.org/What-We-Do/Railbelt-Energy/Bradley-Lake-Hydroelectric-Project), primary document, 2026-08-04.
- The Bradley Lake project began operating in 1991 and delivers power at a cost of about four cents per kilowatt hour. [Alaska Energy Authority](https://www.akenergyauthority.org/What-We-Do/Railbelt-Energy/Bradley-Lake-Hydroelectric-Project), primary document, 2026-08-04.
- The Alaska Energy Authority board of directors endorsed a financing package for constructing the Bradley Lake Expansion Project on July 23, 2026. [Alaska Energy Authority](https://www.akenergyauthority.org/Who-We-Are/Newsroom/Press-Releases), primary document, 2026-07-23.
- The Department of the Air Force is offering approximately 4,700 acres of underutilized land across Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station for potential AI data center development. [U.S. Department of the Air Force](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/4456660/daf-takes-steps-for-potential-alaskan-ai-data-centers/), primary document, 2026-04-10.
- The Air Force has identified twelve parcels at the three Alaska installations for potential AI data center development. [U.S. Department of the Air Force](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/4456660/daf-takes-steps-for-potential-alaskan-ai-data-centers/), primary document, 2026-04-10.
- Robert Moriarty, Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Installations, said the Alaska land offer supports the growing demands of the AI industry while generating value that directly supports Air Force missions. [U.S. Department of the Air Force](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/4456660/daf-takes-steps-for-potential-alaskan-ai-data-centers/), primary document, 2026-04-10.
- Petroleum News reports the Dixon Diversion would move water to Bradley Lake through a 4.6 mile connecting tunnel. [Petroleum News](https://www.petroleumnews.com/story/2026/08/02/news/aea-final-amendment-application-for-bradley-lake-filed-with-ferc/50288.html), report, 2026-08-02.
- Petroleum News reports the expansion would produce enough additional renewable energy to power up to 30,000 homes. [Petroleum News](https://www.petroleumnews.com/story/2026/08/02/news/aea-final-amendment-application-for-bradley-lake-filed-with-ferc/50288.html), report, 2026-08-02.
- Petroleum News reports the expansion would displace around 1.5 billion cubic feet of natural gas per year for power generation. [Petroleum News](https://www.petroleumnews.com/story/2026/08/02/news/aea-final-amendment-application-for-bradley-lake-filed-with-ferc/50288.html), report, 2026-08-02.
- Petroleum News reports that five Railbelt electric utilities receive Bradley Lake power across the transmission system. [Petroleum News](https://www.petroleumnews.com/story/2026/08/02/news/aea-final-amendment-application-for-bradley-lake-filed-with-ferc/50288.html), report, 2026-08-02.
- Air Force solicitation AFCEC-26-R-0006 for AI data center development at the three Alaska installations was posted April 10, 2026, closed to proposals June 29, 2026, and was archived July 14, 2026 with no award posted. [HigherGov (mirror of SAM.gov)](https://www.highergov.com/contract-opportunity/rflp-artificial-intelligence-ai-data-center-deve-afcec-26-r-0006-o-db695/), report, 2026-07-14.
- Alaska Public Media reported that Enstar has already had to turn away new large scale customers to focus on supplying existing ratepayers. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/economy/energy/2026-07-28/southcentral-alaska-gas-utility-says-bills-likely-to-rise-amid-supply-shortage), report, 2026-07-28.
- Enstar president John Sims said that if Southcentral Alaska has a winter like last year, the region is going to have significant challenges and will likely see rolling blackouts. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/economy/energy/2026-07-28/southcentral-alaska-gas-utility-says-bills-likely-to-rise-amid-supply-shortage), report, 2026-07-28.
- Applying the application's approximately 38 percent projected increase to Bradley Lake's 392,000 megawatt hour historical annual average implies roughly 149,000 additional megawatt hours a year, a figure calculated by Alaska.Ai rather than published by any party. [Alaska Energy Authority, arithmetic by Alaska.Ai](https://www.akenergyauthority.org/What-We-Do/Railbelt-Energy/Bradley-Lake-Hydroelectric-Project), report, 2026-08-04.

Slides and the deck PDF are linked from the canonical page.

# A Clause, and a Pit 1.1 Miles Wide

> AI supply chain here means one item on a five item list.

Published 2026-08-03 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-08-03/

## What we verified

- Graphite One's July 22, 2026 release names artificial intelligence infrastructure among the end markets natural graphite supports. [Graphite One Inc. via PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/graphite-one-highlights-strategic-alignment-with-white-house-executive-order-reinforcing-us-critical-minerals-supply-chain-302831679.html), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- The same release says Graphite One's anode materials are aimed primarily at the lithium-ion electric vehicle battery and energy storage markets. [Graphite One Inc. via PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/graphite-one-highlights-strategic-alignment-with-white-house-executive-order-reinforcing-us-critical-minerals-supply-chain-302831679.html), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- President Trump signed an executive order titled Securing America's Defense Supply Chains and Ensuring Domestic Acquisition of Critical Materials on July 20, 2026. [The White House](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/07/securing-americas-defense-supply-chains-and-ensuring-domestic-acquisition-of-critical-materials/), primary document, 2026-07-20.
- Graphite One says it has received two Letters of Interest for $2.07 billion in financing from the EXIM Bank. [Graphite One Inc. via PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/graphite-one-highlights-strategic-alignment-with-white-house-executive-order-reinforcing-us-critical-minerals-supply-chain-302831679.html), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- Graphite One says its domestic supply chain strategy has received U.S. government support in the form of two Department of War grants. [Graphite One Inc. via PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/graphite-one-highlights-strategic-alignment-with-white-house-executive-order-reinforcing-us-critical-minerals-supply-chain-302831679.html), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- Graphite One states that Graphite Creek hosts America's largest known natural graphite deposit. [Graphite One Inc. via PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/graphite-one-highlights-strategic-alignment-with-white-house-executive-order-reinforcing-us-critical-minerals-supply-chain-302831679.html), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- Graphite One's planned Ohio anode facility is in Conneaut, and the Ohio EPA determined its air permit application complete and commenced technical review in July 2026. [Graphite One Inc.](https://www.graphiteoneinc.com/graphite-one-clears-key-ohio-epa-hurdle-for-planned-ohio-battery-materials-facility/), primary document, 2026-07-16.
- About 80 people attended the July 28, 2026 community meeting in Brevig Mission, hosted jointly by the Native Village of Brevig Mission, the City of Brevig Mission and the Brevig Mission Native Corp. [KNOM](https://knom.org/2026/07/30/brevig-mission-residents-oppose-graphite-one-mine-at-community-meeting/), report, 2026-07-30.
- KNOM reported that Brevig Mission residents voiced overwhelming opposition to the proposed Graphite One mine at the meeting. [KNOM](https://knom.org/2026/07/30/brevig-mission-residents-oppose-graphite-one-mine-at-community-meeting/), report, 2026-07-30.
- Brevig Mission is a village of about 400 people and the proposed mine site is about an hour by boat away. [KNOM](https://knom.org/2026/07/30/brevig-mission-residents-oppose-graphite-one-mine-at-community-meeting/), report, 2026-07-30.
- The proposed mine would be a roughly 1.1 mile wide open pit on state land near the Kigluaik Mountains and the Imuruk Basin. [KNOM](https://knom.org/2026/07/30/brevig-mission-residents-oppose-graphite-one-mine-at-community-meeting/), report, 2026-07-30.
- The current proposal estimates a 20 year mine life, with the possibility of an extension. [KNOM](https://knom.org/2026/07/30/brevig-mission-residents-oppose-graphite-one-mine-at-community-meeting/), report, 2026-07-30.
- Graphite One says the project could employ about 250 skilled workers. [KNOM](https://knom.org/2026/07/30/brevig-mission-residents-oppose-graphite-one-mine-at-community-meeting/), report, 2026-07-30.
- The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers said it needs a full Environmental Impact Statement instead of the lesser Environmental Assessment, delaying federal permitting, which had been expected to wrap up this fall, by at least a year. [KNOM](https://knom.org/2026/07/30/brevig-mission-residents-oppose-graphite-one-mine-at-community-meeting/), report, 2026-07-30.
- Bering Straits Native Corporation has invested about $2 million in the project, and with the investment came a seat on a project advisory board. [KNOM](https://knom.org/2026/07/30/brevig-mission-residents-oppose-graphite-one-mine-at-community-meeting/), report, 2026-07-30.
- In November, Brevig Mission's tribe, native corporation and city passed a joint resolution opposing the mine, citing concerns for subsistence resources, cultural integrity, community wellbeing, and long-term sustainability for the region. [KNOM](https://knom.org/2026/07/30/brevig-mission-residents-oppose-graphite-one-mine-at-community-meeting/), report, 2026-07-30.
- Graphite One Chief Operating Officer Mike Schaffner told the meeting, if we can't put a mine in that honors what you just said, there shouldn't be a mine put in. [KNOM](https://knom.org/2026/07/30/brevig-mission-residents-oppose-graphite-one-mine-at-community-meeting/), report, 2026-07-30.
- Darla Tocktoo, tribal office coordinator for the Native Village of Brevig Mission, told Graphite One representatives, I know you really want to dig this mine up for your own money, but we are stopping you for our survival. [KNOM](https://knom.org/2026/07/30/brevig-mission-residents-oppose-graphite-one-mine-at-community-meeting/), report, 2026-07-30.

# What the Notice Buys and What It Doesn't Print

> "Leverage technology, such as artificial intelligence," says an order the governor signed last August.

Published 2026-08-02 by Alaska AI. 10 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-08-02/

## The story

One state contract. Every court, borough and tribe may use it.

This is all the notice says the work is.

"provide all transcription services for general, medical, and legal records to convert speech; either live or recorded, into written or electronic text document."

Eight kinds of public body, one contract.

Three Alaska windows close this month.

3,967 acres at Eielson. Four sites, one total.

The Air Force calls it mixed-use development and names six possible uses. Compute is not one of the six, and the announcement doesn't rule it out either.

Five terms searched. None in the notice.

The DMV asked the same way.

"products, services, technical approaches, and industry best practices related to automated compliance and data integration systems" The word doing the work is automated.

One state document prints it plainly.

"Leverage technology, such as artificial intelligence ("AI"), to support digitization, automation, and public access to permitting information."

The order that names it posts to the same system as the notices that don't.

Administrative Order 360 sends its agency plans to the Alaska Online Public Notice System. So do the two solicitations.

Read the notice before 24 August.

RFP 2026-0200-0064 is public. So is the DMV request. If your borough, court, school district or tribe is in scope, the only way to know what you are inside of is to read it.

## What we verified

- The Alaska statewide transcription solicitation is numbered 2026-0200-0064 and is titled Statewide Transcription Services. [Alaska Online Public Notice System, Department of Administration Office of Procurement and Property Management](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224684), primary document, 2026-07-31.
- The statewide transcription notice was published on the Alaska Online Public Notice System on July 31, 2026. [Alaska Online Public Notice System](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224684), primary document, 2026-07-31.
- The transcription solicitation asks a contractor to convert speech either live or recorded into written or electronic text. [Alaska Online Public Notice System, Office of Procurement and Property Management](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224684), primary document, 2026-07-31.
- The resulting transcription contract may be used by the Alaska Legislative Branch, the Alaska Court System, the University of Alaska, boards and commissions, cities, boroughs, school districts and federally recognized tribes. [Alaska Online Public Notice System, Office of Procurement and Property Management](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224684), primary document, 2026-07-31.
- The public notice text for the statewide transcription solicitation does not contain the terms artificial intelligence, machine learning, automated speech recognition, ASR or AI. [Alaska Online Public Notice System](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224684), primary document, 2026-07-31.
- Proposals for the statewide transcription solicitation are due at 9:30 A.M. Alaska Daylight Time on Monday, August 24, 2026. [Alaska Online Public Notice System](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224684), primary document, 2026-07-31.
- The procurement officer named on the statewide transcription solicitation is Joshua Hartman. [Alaska Online Public Notice System](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224684), primary document, 2026-07-31.
- The Alaska Division of Motor Vehicles published a request for information numbered 02-101-27 on the subject Automatic Compliance and Data Integration CDL. [Alaska Online Public Notice System, Department of Administration Division of Motor Vehicles](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224673), primary document, 2026-07-30.
- The DMV request for information seeks products, services, technical approaches, and industry best practices related to automated compliance and data integration systems. [Alaska Online Public Notice System, Division of Motor Vehicles](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224673), primary document, 2026-07-30.
- The DMV request for information public notice does not contain the terms artificial intelligence, machine learning or AI. [Alaska Online Public Notice System](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224673), primary document, 2026-07-30.
- The DMV request for information was published on July 30, 2026 and responses are due August 20, 2026 at 2:00pm. [Alaska Online Public Notice System](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224673), primary document, 2026-07-30.
- Administrative Order No. 360 was signed by Governor Mike Dunleavy on the 4th day of August 2025. [Office of the Governor, State of Alaska](https://gov.alaska.gov/admin-orders/administrative-order-no-360/), primary document, 2025-08-04.
- Administrative Order No. 360 directs agencies to leverage technology such as artificial intelligence to support digitization, automation, and public access to permitting information. [Office of the Governor, State of Alaska](https://gov.alaska.gov/admin-orders/administrative-order-no-360/), primary document, 2025-08-04.
- Administrative Order No. 360 sets a target of reducing regulatory requirements by 15 percent by December 31, 2026 and by 25 percent cumulative by December 31, 2027. [Office of the Governor, State of Alaska](https://gov.alaska.gov/admin-orders/administrative-order-no-360/), primary document, 2025-08-04.
- Administrative Order No. 360 requires the Department of Law to compile approved agency plans into a single State Unified Regulatory Plan and post it on the Alaska Online Public Notice System. [Office of the Governor, State of Alaska](https://gov.alaska.gov/admin-orders/administrative-order-no-360/), primary document, 2025-08-04.
- The Office of the Governor published its AO 360 Regulatory Reform Plan on the Alaska Online Public Notice System on July 27, 2026. [Alaska Online Public Notice System, Office of the Governor](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224623), primary document, 2026-07-27.
- The Board of Real Estate Appraisers noticed an AO 360 regulations committee meeting on July 28, 2026 for a meeting held August 6, 2026. [Alaska Online Public Notice System, Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development, Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224640), primary document, 2026-07-28.
- The Air Force Civil Engineer Center and the 354th Fighter Wing have identified four distinct sites at Eielson Air Force Base totaling 3,967 acres for potential development. [Eielson Air Force Base, AFIMSC Public Affairs](https://www.eielson.af.mil/News/Display/Article/4550770/air-force-to-host-virtual-industry-day-for-eielson-air-force-base/), primary document, 2026-07-20.
