[Eielson Air Force Base and Air Force Civil Engineer Center](https://www.eielson.af.mil/News/Display/Article/4550770/air-force-to-host-virtual-industry-day-for-eielson-air-force-base/), primary document, 2026-07-20.
- The Eielson announcement describes the proposed project as a mixed-use development combining functions such as residential, commercial, office, cultural, institutional or entertainment. [Eielson Air Force Base, AFIMSC Public Affairs](https://www.eielson.af.mil/News/Display/Article/4550770/air-force-to-host-virtual-industry-day-for-eielson-air-force-base/), primary document, 2026-07-20.

# Where Are the 3,048? The Map Alaska Hasn't Drawn

> If a state letter about your citizenship came and you set it aside, your registration stays inactive.

Published 2026-08-01 by Alaska AI. 10 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-08-01/

## What we verified

- The State of Alaska Office of the Lieutenant Governor refers to the August 18 primary ballot in an official release. [Alaska Office of the Lieutenant Governor](https://ltgov.alaska.gov/newsroom/2026/06/lt-governor-nancy-dahlstrom-opens-investigation-to-determine-validity-of-dan-j-sullivan-filing-for-u-s-senate/), primary document, 2026-06-08.
- The Department of the Air Force is offering approximately 4,700 acres of underutilized land across Joint Base Elmendorf Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station. [U.S. Department of the Air Force](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/4456660/daf-takes-steps-for-potential-alaskan-ai-data-centers/), primary document, 2026-04-10.
- Twelve parcels have been identified for potential development under the Air Force enhanced use lease model. [U.S. Department of the Air Force](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/4456660/daf-takes-steps-for-potential-alaskan-ai-data-centers/), primary document, 2026-04-10.
- The Alaska Division of Elections checks its voter list against Division of Motor Vehicles data every three months, and the check usually returns about 200 names. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/2026-07-23/state-removes-3-500-alaskans-from-voter-rolls-based-in-part-on-old-data), report, 2026-07-23.
- Elections Director Carol Beecher said the division sent a letter to about 3,500 Alaskans after the most recent list comparison. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/2026-07-23/state-removes-3-500-alaskans-from-voter-rolls-based-in-part-on-old-data), report, 2026-07-23.
- A Division of Elections spokesman gave the specific figure of 3,048. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/2026-07-23/state-removes-3-500-alaskans-from-voter-rolls-based-in-part-on-old-data), report, 2026-07-23.
- The Division of Elections moved 3,048 voters to the inactive list over questions about their citizenship. [KMXT / Alaska Public Media (Liz Ruskin)](https://www.kmxt.org/alaska-statewide-news/2026-07-30/23-alaska-legislators-ask-state-to-restore-voters-wrongfully-removed-from-the-rolls), report, 2026-07-30.
- Carol Beecher said some of the data behind the flags is probably very old data from people who never told DMV they had naturalized. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/2026-07-23/state-removes-3-500-alaskans-from-voter-rolls-based-in-part-on-old-data), report, 2026-07-23.
- Beecher acknowledged the old-data problem to legislators at a hearing in Anchorage on Wednesday, July 22, 2026. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/2026-07-23/state-removes-3-500-alaskans-from-voter-rolls-based-in-part-on-old-data), report, 2026-07-23.
- Beecher said people who got the letter can check a box to indicate they are citizens, or call or email the division. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/2026-07-23/state-removes-3-500-alaskans-from-voter-rolls-based-in-part-on-old-data), report, 2026-07-23.
- Beecher said voters who do not respond to the letter will remain on the inactive list. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/2026-07-23/state-removes-3-500-alaskans-from-voter-rolls-based-in-part-on-old-data), report, 2026-07-23.
- Beecher said affected voters can still vote a questioned ballot, attesting that they are a citizen and a valid voter. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/2026-07-23/state-removes-3-500-alaskans-from-voter-rolls-based-in-part-on-old-data), report, 2026-07-23.
- Rep. Andrew Gray told Beecher that the people contacting his office are actual citizens receiving the notice. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/2026-07-23/state-removes-3-500-alaskans-from-voter-rolls-based-in-part-on-old-data), report, 2026-07-23.
- Rep. Kevin McCabe defended the division, saying keeping the voter rolls clean and correct is what it is supposed to do. [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/2026-07-23/state-removes-3-500-alaskans-from-voter-rolls-based-in-part-on-old-data), report, 2026-07-23.
- A bipartisan group of 23 legislators wrote to Beecher asking that all names be put back on the active voters list unless ineligibility has been established. [KMXT / Alaska Public Media (Liz Ruskin)](https://www.kmxt.org/alaska-statewide-news/2026-07-30/23-alaska-legislators-ask-state-to-restore-voters-wrongfully-removed-from-the-rolls), report, 2026-07-30.
- Alaska's News Source reported the letter was signed by 20 members of the bipartisan majority. [Alaska's News Source](https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/07/30/lawmakers-say-elections-division-illegally-deactivated-registration-thousands-voters-urges-director-reverse-decision/), report, 2026-07-29.
- The legislators' letter says they have heard from numerous citizens whose voting rights have been cancelled illegally and without just cause. [Alaska's News Source](https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/07/30/lawmakers-say-elections-division-illegally-deactivated-registration-thousands-voters-urges-director-reverse-decision/), report, 2026-07-29.
- The legislators' letter says the division's actions threaten to deprive Alaskans of their most fundamental right in a democracy and that the mistakes should be addressed immediately. [KMXT / Alaska Public Media (Liz Ruskin)](https://www.kmxt.org/alaska-statewide-news/2026-07-30/23-alaska-legislators-ask-state-to-restore-voters-wrongfully-removed-from-the-rolls), report, 2026-07-30.
- Rep. Ky Holland helped organize the letter and said there is not much time to correct the mistakes because the August 18 primary is just weeks away. [KMXT / Alaska Public Media (Liz Ruskin)](https://www.kmxt.org/alaska-statewide-news/2026-07-30/23-alaska-legislators-ask-state-to-restore-voters-wrongfully-removed-from-the-rolls), report, 2026-07-30.
- A joint Division of Elections and DMV statement said Elections most recently asked DMV to compare lists in March 2026, which produced the letters. [Alaska's News Source](https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/07/30/lawmakers-say-elections-division-illegally-deactivated-registration-thousands-voters-urges-director-reverse-decision/), report, 2026-07-29.
- The joint Division of Elections and DMV statement said all the qualified voters who received these letters can still vote in the upcoming elections. [Alaska's News Source](https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/07/30/lawmakers-say-elections-division-illegally-deactivated-registration-thousands-voters-urges-director-reverse-decision/), report, 2026-07-29.
- House Minority Leader DeLena Johnson said that if a voter's records indicate they are not a U.S. citizen, flagging that record for review is a reasonable and responsible step. [Alaska's News Source](https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/07/30/lawmakers-say-elections-division-illegally-deactivated-registration-thousands-voters-urges-director-reverse-decision/), report, 2026-07-29.
- As of July 30 the Division of Elections had not answered specific questions about the legislators' letter, and a spokesman said the division would respond. [KMXT / Alaska Public Media (Liz Ruskin)](https://www.kmxt.org/alaska-statewide-news/2026-07-30/23-alaska-legislators-ask-state-to-restore-voters-wrongfully-removed-from-the-rolls), report, 2026-07-30.
- Jeannie McLeod, 75, of Anchorage said that when she became a citizen in 2024 she legally changed her first name from Emily to Jeannie, the name she has always used. [KMXT / Alaska Public Media (Liz Ruskin)](https://www.kmxt.org/alaska-statewide-news/2026-07-30/23-alaska-legislators-ask-state-to-restore-voters-wrongfully-removed-from-the-rolls), report, 2026-07-30.
- Jeannie McLeod said she was mailed a voter's card carrying her old name and asked why the state would take her off and reinstate her under a name that is not legally hers. [KMXT / Alaska Public Media (Liz Ruskin)](https://www.kmxt.org/alaska-statewide-news/2026-07-30/23-alaska-legislators-ask-state-to-restore-voters-wrongfully-removed-from-the-rolls), report, 2026-07-30.
- KMXT reported that some affected voters got their driver's licenses before they were citizens and registered to vote after becoming citizens. [KMXT / Alaska Public Media (Liz Ruskin)](https://www.kmxt.org/alaska-statewide-news/2026-07-30/23-alaska-legislators-ask-state-to-restore-voters-wrongfully-removed-from-the-rolls), report, 2026-07-30.

# Struck. And Still Printed. Alaska's $500 Cap

> Alaska's statute, as codified, still prints a $500 cap on giving to a candidate.

Published 2026-07-31 by Alaska AI. 10 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-31/

## What we verified

- The Alaska Public Offices Commission's own published contribution limits table lists what an individual Alaska resident may give a candidate as Unlimited. [Alaska Public Offices Commission](https://apoc.doa.alaska.gov/filer-resources/contribution-limits/), primary document, 2026-07-29.
- The same APOC table lists a non resident individual's limit to an Alaska candidate as Unlimited, identical to an Alaska resident's. [Alaska Public Offices Commission](https://apoc.doa.alaska.gov/filer-resources/contribution-limits/), primary document, 2026-07-29.
- APOC's contribution limits page carried a July 29, 2026 date stamp, two days before this run and twenty days before the primary. [Alaska Public Offices Commission](https://apoc.doa.alaska.gov/filer-resources/contribution-limits/), primary document, 2026-07-29.
- The same APOC table lists a group based outside Alaska as Prohibited from giving to a candidate, while listing a non resident individual as Unlimited. [Alaska Public Offices Commission](https://apoc.doa.alaska.gov/filer-resources/contribution-limits/), primary document, 2026-07-29.
- The Ninth Circuit decided Thompson v. Hebdon on July 30, 2021. [United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit](https://cdn.ca9.uscourts.gov/datastore/opinions/2021/07/30/17-35019.pdf), primary document, 2021-07-30.
- The Ninth Circuit reversed the district court on the individual to candidate limit, the individual to group limit and the nonresident aggregate limit, while upholding the political party to candidate limit. [United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit](https://cdn.ca9.uscourts.gov/datastore/opinions/2021/07/30/17-35019.pdf), primary document, 2021-07-30.
- The Ninth Circuit opinion identifies the struck provision as the $500 annual limit on an individual contribution to a political candidate at Alaska Stat. section 15.13.070(b)(1). [United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit](https://cdn.ca9.uscourts.gov/datastore/opinions/2021/07/30/17-35019.pdf), primary document, 2021-07-30.
- The Ninth Circuit held that Alaska's aggregate nonresident contribution limit violates the First Amendment. [United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit](https://cdn.ca9.uscourts.gov/datastore/opinions/2021/07/30/17-35019.pdf), primary document, 2021-07-30.
- Lead plaintiff David Thompson sent candidate Wes Keller a $100 check in 2015 and the campaign returned it because it had already hit the $3,000 nonresident limit. [United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit](https://cdn.ca9.uscourts.gov/datastore/opinions/2021/07/30/17-35019.pdf), primary document, 2021-07-30.
- Ballot Measure 1 appears on Alaska's August 18, 2026 primary ballot. [Alaska Division of Elections](https://www.elections.alaska.gov/election/2026/Primary/SampleBallots/HD1.pdf), primary document, 2026-07-31.
- The printed ballot text says individuals could give $2,000 to candidates and $5,000 to political parties. [Alaska Division of Elections](https://www.elections.alaska.gov/election/2026/Primary/SampleBallots/HD1.pdf), primary document, 2026-07-31.
- The printed ballot text also says groups besides political parties could give $4,000 to candidates and that individuals could give $4,000 to joint campaigns for governor and lieutenant governor. [Alaska Division of Elections](https://www.elections.alaska.gov/election/2026/Primary/SampleBallots/HD1.pdf), primary document, 2026-07-31.
- The ballot text says the new limits would increase with inflation every ten years beginning in 2031. [Alaska Division of Elections](https://www.elections.alaska.gov/election/2026/Primary/SampleBallots/HD1.pdf), primary document, 2026-07-31.
- The Alaska Constitution provides that an initiated law becomes effective ninety days after certification. [Office of the Lieutenant Governor of Alaska, Alaska Constitution Article XI Section 6](https://ltgov.alaska.gov/information/alaskas-constitution/), primary document, 2026-07-31.
- The same constitutional section provides that the lieutenant governor certifies the election returns. [Office of the Lieutenant Governor of Alaska, Alaska Constitution Article XI Section 6](https://ltgov.alaska.gov/information/alaskas-constitution/), primary document, 2026-07-31.
- Alaskans passed the $500 contribution cap themselves at the August 22, 2006 primary election by 113,130 votes to 41,836. [Alaska Division of Elections, official 2006 primary election results](https://www.elections.alaska.gov/results/06PRIM/data/results.htm), primary document, 2006-08-22.
- The 2006 measure and the 2026 measure both reached voters on an August primary ballot, twenty years apart, and both were numbered Ballot Measure 1. [Alaska Division of Elections](https://www.elections.alaska.gov/results/06PRIM/data/results.htm), primary document, 2006-08-22.
- Drake Thomas wrote that he is terrified by the pace of AI development and wishes it were slower. [Anchorage Daily News opinion, Drake Thomas](https://www.adn.com/opinions/2026/07/29/opinion-why-this-anthropic-employee-gave-100k-to-a-candidate-for-alaska-governor/), primary document, 2026-07-29.
- Drake Thomas wrote that it is crazy that Alaska allows unlimited contributions and that he hopes that changes. [Anchorage Daily News opinion, Drake Thomas](https://www.adn.com/opinions/2026/07/29/opinion-why-this-anthropic-employee-gave-100k-to-a-candidate-for-alaska-governor/), primary document, 2026-07-29.
- The op-ed's author bio says Drake Thomas grew up in Kenai and that the views are his alone and do not represent Anthropic. [Anchorage Daily News opinion, Drake Thomas](https://www.adn.com/opinions/2026/07/29/opinion-why-this-anthropic-employee-gave-100k-to-a-candidate-for-alaska-governor/), primary document, 2026-07-29.
- Thomas wrote that he works on the safety team at Anthropic and develops reports about the risks of AI models. [Anchorage Daily News opinion, Drake Thomas](https://www.adn.com/opinions/2026/07/29/opinion-why-this-anthropic-employee-gave-100k-to-a-candidate-for-alaska-governor/), primary document, 2026-07-29.

# Alaska's One Row on the Federal AI List

> Enstar is warning about rolling blackouts and fielding new data center interest in the same week.

Published 2026-07-30 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-30/

## What we verified

- The Department of Energy announced 278 projects selected in the first round of Genesis Mission awards. [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/articles/secretary-energy-chris-wright-announces-first-genesis-mission-projects-selected-accelerate), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- Exactly one of the 278 award rows is an Alaska institution, a University of Alaska Fairbanks project led by Richard Wies and titled AURORA-AI, Alaska Utility Resilience and Optimization using Real-time AI. [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2026-07/GM-RFA-Awards-List.pdf), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- The Genesis Mission awards list was posted by the Department of Energy on July 22, 2026. [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2026-07/GM-RFA-Awards-List.pdf), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- The Genesis Mission projects involve 342 participating institutions, made up of 16 Department of Energy and NNSA National Laboratories, 142 universities, 157 companies, 13 nonprofit organizations and 14 other institutions. [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/articles/secretary-energy-chris-wright-announces-first-genesis-mission-projects-selected-accelerate), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- The Department of Energy said the Genesis Mission funding call generated the largest response to a funding opportunity in its history. [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/articles/secretary-energy-chris-wright-announces-first-genesis-mission-projects-selected-accelerate), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- Energy Secretary Chris Wright said America has no shortage of bold ideas or talented scientists and that the response to the Genesis Mission proves it. [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/articles/secretary-energy-chris-wright-announces-first-genesis-mission-projects-selected-accelerate), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- The largest single project selected in the first Genesis Mission round is a three year 60 million dollar investment in nuclear energy. [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/articles/secretary-energy-chris-wright-announces-first-genesis-mission-projects-selected-accelerate), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- The National Laboratory of the Rockies announced 12 Genesis Mission projects in a release whose headline names Alaska utility optimization. [National Laboratory of the Rockies via GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/22/3331669/0/en/nlr-awarded-12-genesis-mission-projects-ranging-from-semiconductors-to-alaska-utility-optimization.html), primary document, 2026-07-22.
- Richard Wies is a Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Alaska Fairbanks. [University of Alaska Fairbanks, Alaska Center for Energy and Power](https://www.uaf.edu/acep/about/our-team/richard-wies.php), primary document, 2026-07-30.
- Richard Wies leads research with the Alaska Center for Energy and Power as an electric power systems expert, working on renewable energy integration in remote islanded microgrids. [University of Alaska Fairbanks, Alaska Center for Energy and Power](https://www.uaf.edu/acep/about/our-team/richard-wies.php), primary document, 2026-07-30.
- The Department of Energy put the number of isolated microgrid systems in Alaska not connected to larger grids at approximately 200, in a 2017 program description. [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/eere/buildings/articles/gmlc-1321-alaska-microgrid-partnership), primary document, 2017-09-14.
- No description of the AURORA-AI project had been published anywhere beyond its title on the award list as of July 30, 2026. [Search result, negative finding verified by the fact-checker](https://www.bing.com/search?q=%22AURORA-AI%22+%22Alaska+Utility+Resilience%22+Wies), report, 2026-07-30.

[Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/economy/energy/2026-07-28/southcentral-alaska-gas-utility-says-bills-likely-to-rise-amid-supply-shortage), report, 2026-07-28.

# The Machine Makes Time. Who Owns the Clock?

> On a Cook Inlet salmon boat this month, a sockeye enters a steel box on deck and leaves it iced.

Published 2026-07-29 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-29/

## The story

Not a better fish. More hours.

Scan. Spike. Cut. Ice. Six and a half seconds.

Computer vision picks the fish and the path. A spike to the hindbrain, a cut at the gills, then into slush ice.

Seven hours becomes sixty. That gap is the product.

A suffocated salmon stiffens in about seven hours. Shinkei says its process pushes that to sixty. Same fish. The only thing added is time, and it is added on an Alaska deck.

Every one of those numbers is the company's own.

None of it has been tested by anyone outside Shinkei. That does not make it false. It makes it unaudited, which is a different thing.

More than 1,300 permits. A handful of boats.

What is not public is how many of these boats are running the robot this season.

The machine is free. The split is not disclosed.

Nobody here is being fleeced. What is not on the record anywhere is the share, and a share you cannot see is hard to bargain over.

The fish stays Alaskan. The asset does not.

Khawaja says the company handles and markets the fish under its own brand. The hours are made on an Alaska deck.

None of it is on a shelf yet.

IntraFish says the retail rollout is expected this summer. On the day this deck was built, the brand's own species list ran to six fish and none of them was salmon.

When the value moves from the fish to the clock, who should own the clock?

## What we verified

- Shinkei Systems announced PSDN-S as its newest harvesting robot created to bring Seremoni Grade handling to Alaska's wild salmon industry. [Shinkei Systems company LinkedIn post](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/shinkeisystems_meet-psdn-s-shinkeis-newest-harvesting-activity-7485731065567981568-f_mm), primary document, 2026-07-23.
- Shinkei says PSDN-S was built to make its harvesting technology more practical for the smaller boats used throughout Alaska's salmon fisheries. [Shinkei Systems company LinkedIn post](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/shinkeisystems_meet-psdn-s-shinkeis-newest-harvesting-activity-7485731065567981568-f_mm), primary document, 2026-07-23.
- Shinkei's website says PSDN extends shelf life 3x. [Shinkei Systems](https://shinkei.systems/), primary document, 2026-07-29.
- The Alaska Department of Fish and Game says more than 1,300 drift and set gillnet limited entry permits exist for the Upper Cook Inlet area. [Alaska Department of Fish and Game](https://www.adfg.alaska.gov/index.cfm?adfg=commercialbyareauci.main), primary document, 2026-07-29.
- The Alaska Department of Fish and Game says sockeye salmon are the most important species by economic value in Upper Cook Inlet. [Alaska Department of Fish and Game](https://www.adfg.alaska.gov/index.cfm?adfg=commercialbyareauci.main), primary document, 2026-07-29.
- NOAA Fisheries says the 2026 commercial fishing season for the Cook Inlet EEZ Area opens on June 22 and closes on or before August 15. [NOAA Fisheries](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/alaska/commercial-fishing/salmon-management-federal-waters-cook-inlet-cook-inlet-eez), primary document, 2026-07-10.
- The Alaska Department of Fish and Game reported the 2025 statewide commercial salmon harvest at 194.8 million fish worth approximately 541 million dollars. [Alaska Department of Fish and Game](https://www.adfg.alaska.gov/index.cfm?adfg=pressreleases.pr&release=2025_11_04), primary document, 2025-11-04.
- IntraFish published an article headlined 'Shinkei rolls out robot-harvested Alaska salmon' on 22 July 2026. [IntraFish](https://www.intrafish.com/salmon/shinkei-rolls-out-robot-harvested-alaska-salmon/2-1-2019898), report, 2026-07-22.
- IntraFish's subhead says Shinkei expects to roll out its Seremoni Grade salmon to select retail and restaurant partners this summer. [IntraFish](https://www.intrafish.com/salmon/shinkei-rolls-out-robot-harvested-alaska-salmon/2-1-2019898), report, 2026-07-22.
- IntraFish's photo caption places Shinkei Systems working with fishermen in Alaska's Cook Inlet in 2026. [IntraFish](https://www.intrafish.com/salmon/shinkei-rolls-out-robot-harvested-alaska-salmon/2-1-2019898), report, 2026-07-22.
- Shinkei chief executive Saif Khawaja said the company owns the machines and puts them on the boats for free. [National Fisherman](https://www.nationalfisherman.com/robots-on-deck), report, 2025-08-06.
- Khawaja said Shinkei splits the proceeds variably with the fishermen it works with. [National Fisherman](https://www.nationalfisherman.com/robots-on-deck), report, 2025-08-06.
- Khawaja said Shinkei handles and markets the fish under its own brand Seremoni Grade. [National Fisherman](https://www.nationalfisherman.com/robots-on-deck), report, 2025-08-06.
- Shinkei's lead mechanical engineer Waiman Meinhold described the deck machine as about the size of a refrigerator. [National Fisherman](https://www.nationalfisherman.com/robots-on-deck), report, 2025-08-06.
- Shinkei says the machine scans a fish, spikes the brain, cuts the gills and puts it into slush ice in 6.5 seconds or less. [National Fisherman](https://www.nationalfisherman.com/robots-on-deck), report, 2025-08-06.
- Khawaja said Shinkei can build a machine every two weeks. [National Fisherman](https://www.nationalfisherman.com/robots-on-deck), report, 2025-08-06.
- The Spoon reported that each fish is processed in about six seconds. [The Spoon](https://thespoon.tech/shinkei-hopes-bringing-robotics-ai-to-the-fishing-boat-leads-to-fresher-fish-and-less-waste/), report, 2025-12-18.
- The Spoon reported that Shinkei uses computer vision AI to scan the fish and determine the fastest and least stressful path forward. [The Spoon](https://thespoon.tech/shinkei-hopes-bringing-robotics-ai-to-the-fishing-boat-leads-to-fresher-fish-and-less-waste/), report, 2025-12-18.
- The Spoon reported that a traditionally suffocated fish enters rigor mortis in about 7 hours while Shinkei's process expands that up to 60 hours. [The Spoon](https://thespoon.tech/shinkei-hopes-bringing-robotics-ai-to-the-fishing-boat-leads-to-fresher-fish-and-less-waste/), report, 2025-12-18.
- The Spoon reported that Shinkei recently raised 22 million dollars in a Series A co-led by Founders Fund and Interlagos. [The Spoon](https://thespoon.tech/shinkei-hopes-bringing-robotics-ai-to-the-fishing-boat-leads-to-fresher-fish-and-less-waste/), report, 2025-12-18.
- The Spoon reported that Shinkei works with eight boats sourcing black cod, rockfish and red snapper. [The Spoon](https://thespoon.tech/shinkei-hopes-bringing-robotics-ai-to-the-fishing-boat-leads-to-fresher-fish-and-less-waste/), report, 2025-12-18.
- Shinkei acquired a 16,000 square foot fish processing facility in Tacoma, Washington from FATHOM Seafood. [SalmonBusiness](https://www.salmonbusiness.com/robot-powered-seafood-firm-shinkei-expands-with-us-west-coast-processing-facility/), report, 2026-03-13.
- The Tacoma plant was reported to open in spring 2026 with a core workforce of more than 50 employees plus seasonal hires. [SalmonBusiness](https://www.salmonbusiness.com/robot-powered-seafood-firm-shinkei-expands-with-us-west-coast-processing-facility/), report, 2026-03-13.
- Shinkei said the Tacoma plant would source fish from fishermen in Alaska, Washington and California. [Robotics and Automation News](https://roboticsandautomationnews.com/2026/03/11/robotic-seafood-company-shinkei-systems-acquires-first-processing-plant-to-scale-nationwide/99505/), report, 2026-03-11.
- Khawaja said NERA uses Shinkei's proprietary datasets to show how fresh each fish is and how many days it can be sold. [Robotics and Automation News](https://roboticsandautomationnews.com/2026/03/11/robotic-seafood-company-shinkei-systems-acquires-first-processing-plant-to-scale-nationwide/99505/), report, 2026-03-11.
- Khawaja told the Los Angeles Times his end goal is grocery shoppers buying fish that lasts three times as long, tastes better and is handled humanely. [Los Angeles Times republished by AOL](https://www.aol.com/news/robot-uses-japanese-tradition-ai-100000819.html), report, 2025-07-29.
- Deckboss reported that the 2025 Upper Cook Inlet sockeye harvest was worth 35.8 million dollars at an estimated average price of 1.73 dollars per pound. [Deckboss, Wesley Loy](https://deckboss.blogspot.com/2025/10/impressive-numbers-for-cook-inlet_02076007099.html), report, 2025-10-24.
- KFSK reported that Silver Bay Seafoods announced a Bristol Bay sockeye base price of 1.60 dollars per pound for the 2026 season. [KFSK CoastAlaska](https://www.kfsk.org/2026/07/15/commercial-salmon-prices-up-this-year-in-alaska/), report, 2026-07-15.
- Trade coverage of the Alaska rollout says Shinkei provides its robots to Alaskan fishermen at no cost while purchasing their catch at premium prices. [RobotToday republishing Leaderobot](https://robottoday.com/industry-briefing/shinkei-systems-introduces-ai-robotics-for-enhanced-fresh-fish-processing/9299), report, 2026-07-23.
- FISHBIO reported Khawaja saying the company is doing the equivalent of surgery on the fish in a very difficult maritime environment. [FISHBIO republishing IntraFish](https://fishbio.com/news/shinkei-rolls-out-robot-harvested-alaska-salmon/), report, 2026-07-23.

# One Line Out. Alaska's One Name on the AI Power Pledge

> Cordova sits on Prince William Sound, off the state highway system, with no transmission line to another community.

Published 2026-07-26 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-26/

## The story

One Alaska utility signed. Its wires reach no one else.

281 names on the pledge. One of them is in Alaska.

Cordova Electric Cooperative is filed under Cooperative on the White House signatory page. No Railbelt utility appears on the list as read.

Five commitments. Nobody has to keep them.

USA TODAY and POWER both call the pledge non binding. Twenty three governors signed an addendum promising to implement its principles to the greatest extent possible.

1,566 customers. 18 megawatts. No line out.

Cordova Electric Cooperative runs one diesel plant and two hydroelectric plants. The town is off the state highway system and the cooperative is not connected by transmission line to any other community.

Every megawatt in this story, on one axis.

It passed the Senate. Then it stopped.

SB 250 would have required commission approved contracts so a data center's infrastructure and service costs are borne by the operator rather than shifted to other customers. It passed the Alaska Senate on May 16, 2026 and died in House Community and Regional Affairs.

A pledge asks. A contract binds.

The other answer is to leave the grid entirely.

Rep. Nick Begich of Alaska introduced the DATA Act on April 21, 2026. He says it lets manufacturers run on fully self contained grid of one power systems.

A promise is not an instrument.

Twenty three governors signed. One Alaska utility signed, as the list read 2026-07-26. Neither signature is a rule.

## What we verified

- Gov. Mike Dunleavy of Alaska is one of 23 Republican governors who signed the Ratepayer Protection Pledge addendum announced on July 23, 2026. [Republican Governors Association](https://www.rga.org/republican-governors-sign-president-trumps-ratepayer-protection-pledge/), primary document, 2026-07-23.
- The pledge preamble states that the American people should not be footing the bill for the benefit of private companies. [Republican Governors Association](https://www.rga.org/republican-governors-sign-president-trumps-ratepayer-protection-pledge/), primary document, 2026-07-23.
- The pledge sets five commitments for signing companies, build bring or buy new power supply, pay for new power delivery infrastructure, pay whether they use the power or not, invest in local jobs and workforce development, and contribute to grid and community resilience. [The White House](https://www.whitehouse.gov/ratepayer-protection-pledge/), primary document, 2026-07-26.
- EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin said the global race for AI is underway and America must win it, but not by asking working families to pay for it. [U.S. Environmental Protection Agency](https://www.epa.gov/newsreleases/president-trump-expands-historic-ratepayer-protection-pledge-protect-american), primary document, 2026-07-23.
- The pledge was first signed on March 4, 2026 by seven AI companies and hyperscalers, Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle and xAI. [U.S. Environmental Protection Agency](https://www.epa.gov/newsreleases/president-trump-expands-historic-ratepayer-protection-pledge-protect-american), primary document, 2026-07-23.
- Read live on July 26, 2026 the White House signatory page counters showed All 281, Cooperatives 176, Utilities 69 and Data Center Developers 35. [The White House](https://www.whitehouse.gov/ratepayer-protection-pledge/), primary document, 2026-07-26.
- Cordova Electric Cooperative is listed as a signatory on the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge page under the Cooperative category. [The White House](https://www.whitehouse.gov/ratepayer-protection-pledge/), primary document, 2026-07-26.
- Cordova Electric Cooperative is located in Cordova, Alaska. [Cordova Electric Cooperative](https://www.cordovaelectric.com/), primary document, 2026-07-26.
- Cordova Electric Cooperative is the only Alaska entity on the White House signatory list as read on July 26, 2026. [The White House](https://www.whitehouse.gov/ratepayer-protection-pledge/), primary document, 2026-07-26.
- Cordova Electric Cooperative serves 1,566 customers. [Cordova Electric Cooperative](https://www.cordovaelectric.com/about/), primary document, 2026-07-26.
- Cordova is not connected by transmission line to other communities. [Cordova Electric Cooperative](https://www.cordovaelectric.com/about/), primary document, 2026-07-26.
- Cordova Electric Cooperative has total generating capacity of 18 megawatts across one diesel plant and two hydroelectric plants. [Cordova Electric Cooperative](https://www.cordovaelectric.com/about/), primary document, 2026-07-26.
- Rep. Nick Begich introduced the House DATA Act of 2026 on April 21, 2026 with Reps. Dan Crenshaw and Burgess Owens as a companion to Senate legislation led by Sen. Tom Cotton. [Office of Rep. Nick Begich](https://begich.house.gov/media/press-releases/congressman-begich-leads-legislation-lower-energy-costs-introduces-house), primary document, 2026-04-21.
- Begich says the DATA Act allows manufacturers to operate on fully self contained grid of one power systems so innovation can scale without forcing households to subsidize massive new energy demands. [Office of Rep. Nick Begich](https://begich.house.gov/media/press-releases/congressman-begich-leads-legislation-lower-energy-costs-introduces-house), primary document, 2026-04-21.
- The Department of the Air Force is offering approximately 4,700 acres across twelve parcels at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station for potential AI data centers. [U.S. Air Force](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/4456660/daf-takes-steps-for-potential-alaskan-ai-data-centers/), primary document, 2026-04-10.
- Robert Moriarty, Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Installations, called the land offering a unique opportunity for a true public private partnership supporting the growing demands of the AI industry. [U.S. Air Force](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/4456660/daf-takes-steps-for-potential-alaskan-ai-data-centers/), primary document, 2026-04-10.
- The governors addendum commits signers to implement the principles established in the Ratepayer Protection Pledge to the greatest extent possible in their respective positions. [USA TODAY via Central Oregon Daily](https://www.centraloregondaily.com/news/nation-world/23-governors-sign-trumps-cost-pledge-for-data-centers-backbone-of-ai/article_0e204a10-f776-5f29-93b4-04f84a68a7eb.html), report, 2026-07-23.
- The pledge is explicitly non binding. [USA TODAY via Central Oregon Daily](https://www.centraloregondaily.com/news/nation-world/23-governors-sign-trumps-cost-pledge-for-data-centers-backbone-of-ai/article_0e204a10-f776-5f29-93b4-04f84a68a7eb.html), report, 2026-07-23.

- The Cordova data center uses only 150 kilowatts and as a pilot project could expand to 3 megawatts and become the cooperative's largest customer. [Fairbanks Daily News-Miner](https://www.newsminer.com/news/alaska_news/air-force-solicits-interest-in-alaska-data-centers-but-faces-some-hurdles/article_4a42264e-cadb-4f1c-a8f4-c74d2b099ba2.html), report, 2026-03-01.
- SB 250 by Sen. Loki Tobin was titled An Act relating to data centers and relating to utility service for data centers, was introduced February 18, 2026 and was marked dead May 20, 2026. [BillTrack50](https://www.billtrack50.com/billdetail/1974439), report, 2026-07-26.
- SB 250 would have required utilities to enter commission approved contracts with data centers so their infrastructure and service costs are borne by the data center operators rather than shifted to other customers. [Davis Wright Tremaine](https://www.dwt.com/blogs/energy--environmental-law-blog/2026/06/alaska-data-center-development-next-steps), report, 2026-06-29.
- SB 250 passed the Alaska Senate on May 16, 2026 and then died in the House Community and Regional Affairs Committee. [Davis Wright Tremaine](https://www.dwt.com/blogs/energy--environmental-law-blog/2026/06/alaska-data-center-development-next-steps), report, 2026-06-29.

Shelley Hughes covered disclosure of election related deepfakes and use of artificial intelligence by state agencies, was introduced January 22, 2025, got one recorded hearing on April 29, 2025 and died. [BillTrack50](https://www.billtrack50.com/billdetail/1775660), report, 2026-07-26.
- An Alaska provision sponsored by Rep. Sarah Vance prohibiting creation or possession of AI generated child sexual abuse material took effect July 1, 2026. [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/politics/alaska-legislature/2026/06/30/education-funding-age-of-consent-and-more-several-alaska-laws-go-into-effect-july-1/), report, 2026-06-30.

# 500 to Fewer Than 12. One Office Holds the Pen.

> More than 500 comments landed on a North Slope AI data center, and fewer than a dozen backed it.

Published 2026-07-24 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-24/

## The story

Form letters lacking substance.

500 said no. One office decides.

A square mile of gravel. 26 miles from Deadhorse.

Bigger than the whole grid.

Not every objection is equal.

Your bill is the weak argument.

The real fight is land, gravel, gas.

Form letters lacking substance.

When 500 say no and fewer than a dozen say yes, should one office hold the pen?

## What we verified

- Alaska DNR's Division of Oil and Gas issued a preliminary decision dated May 12, 2026 regarding the Stak Energy lease (ADL 422741). [Alaska DNR Online Public Notices (ADL 422741)](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=223817), report, 2026-05-12.
- The decision would grant STAK Energy Corporation a 50-year lease of 715.4 acres of state land. [Alaska DNR Online Public Notices](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=223817), report, 2026-05-12.
- The site is located adjacent to the Dalton Highway approximately 26 miles south of Deadhorse. [Alaska DNR Online Public Notices](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=223817), report, 2026-05-12.
- The site is near Dalton Highway Milepost 390. [Northern Alaska Environmental Center](https://northern.org/news/stak-energy-campus-what-the-states-lease-documents-reveal-about-scale-risk-and-unanswered-questions/), report, 2026-05-28.
- The proposed use is a commercial natural-gas-powered energy facility including modular high-performance computing (AI data center) units. [Alaska DNR Online Public Notices](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=223817), report, 2026-05-12.
- The project proposes 1 to 3 gigawatts of on-site natural-gas-fired generation. [Northern Alaska Environmental Center](https://northern.org/news/stak-energy-campus-what-the-states-lease-documents-reveal-about-scale-risk-and-unanswered-questions/), report, 2026-05-28.
- The facility would consume 350 to 500 million standard cubic feet of gas per day, roughly 128 to 183 billion cubic feet per year. [Northern Alaska Environmental Center](https://northern.org/news/stak-energy-campus-what-the-states-lease-documents-reveal-about-scale-risk-and-unanswered-questions/), report, 2026-05-28.
- Reported cost is about $500 million for initial site development and more than $10 billion for the total project. [Northern Alaska Environmental Center](https://northern.org/news/stak-energy-campus-what-the-states-lease-documents-reveal-about-scale-risk-and-unanswered-questions/), report, 2026-05-28.
- Site work includes a principal gravel pad of approximately 640 acres, a 1.8-mile gravel access road, and roughly 7.1 million cubic yards of gravel fill. [Northern Alaska Environmental Center](https://northern.org/news/stak-energy-campus-what-the-states-lease-documents-reveal-about-scale-risk-and-unanswered-questions/), report, 2026-05-28.
- The public comment window originally closed at 4:30 p.m. Alaska Daylight Time on June 15, 2026, and was extended to July 17, 2026 due to comment volume. [Alaska DNR Online Public Notices](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=223817), report, 2026-05-12.
- More than 500 public comments were received, with fewer than a dozen in support of the project. [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/business-economy/2026/07/07/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-07.
- Stak Chief Strategy Officer John Boyle, a former Alaska DNR commissioner, said the vast majority of comments are form letters lacking substance. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- The generators could produce a gigawatt or more, roughly 30% more than the peak demand of urban Alaska's entire grid. [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/business-economy/2026/07/07/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-07.

Slides and the deck PDF are linked from the canonical page.

# Governed First, Alaska Native Health and AI

> Data sovereignty is not a privacy setting.

Published 2026-07-23 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-23/

## The story

In Alaska Native health, the Tribe decides what AI runs.

Sovereignty means the Tribe governs its own data.

In Alaska, that record is life and death.

One is live. One is proposed.

Two rule sets, one authority.

Alaska Native institutions convened this.

In 2022, a third had never heard of AI.

This rests on one paper.

Adopt fast. Govern first.

## What we verified

- A symposium-perspectives paper on AI/ML in Alaska Native healthcare was published May 23, 2026 in the International Journal of Circumpolar Health (doi 10.1080/22423982.2026.2677426). [International Journal of Circumpolar Health (via PMC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13202658/), primary document.
- The 2025 Anchorage symposium had 31 participants. [IJCH (via PMC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13202658/), primary document.
- Symposium participants by organization, ANTHC 38%, Southcentral Foundation 27%, Maniilaq Association 15%, Stanford 8%, CDC Arctic Investigation Program 8%, Other 4%. [IJCH (via PMC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13202658/), primary document.
- Symposium participants by role, researchers 27%, IT/programming 24%, leadership 17%, clinicians 12%, compliance 5%, other 15%. [IJCH (via PMC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13202658/), primary document.
- Alaska's air-evacuation rates are cited as at least 40 times higher than anywhere else in the US. [IJCH (via PMC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13202658/), primary document.
- Over 80% of Alaska communities are not connected to the road system. [IJCH (via PMC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13202658/), primary document.
- In the 2022 baseline, 35% of respondents said they had never heard the term AI/ML. [IJCH (via PMC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13202658/), primary document.
- The paper reports that overall knowledge, use, and awareness of AI/ML increased substantially between the 2022 and 2025 symposia. [IJCH (via PMC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13202658/), primary document.
- The governance approach references the CARE principles (Collective Benefit, Authority to Control, Responsibility, Ethics) and the FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable). [IJCH (via PMC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13202658/), primary document.
- The system operates under Indigenous data sovereignty, the right of a federally recognized Tribe to govern the collection, ownership, and use of its own data. [IJCH (via PMC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13202658/), primary document.
- A rural tribal health organization has implemented a Cerner AI Scribe in primary care visits. [IJCH (via PMC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13202658/), primary document.
- ANTHC shared a statewide organizational AI use policy. [IJCH (via PMC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13202658/), primary document.
- A medevac decision-support model is under development (proposed, not yet deployed). [IJCH (via PMC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13202658/), primary document.
- The paper's authors span Southcentral Foundation, Stanford University, the Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium, and Maniilaq Association. [IJCH (via PMC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13202658/), primary document.
- A companion community-engaged AI framework paper for the Alaska Tribal Health System was published April 7, 2025 in Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence. [Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence (via PMC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12009764/), primary document.

Slides and the deck PDF are linked from the canonical page.

# The Giveaway, Surveyed. Alaska's Free Land for AI

> Alaska is moving to hand 31 square miles of public land to its own development agency for zero dollars.

Published 2026-07-22 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-22/

## The story

31 SQUARE / MILES OF / PUBLIC LAND. / FREE.

The state moved to give it to its own development agency.

19,950 acres. / No price.

Under a preliminary decision, a state agency would convey about 19,950 acres of public land, roughly 31 square miles, to AIDEA, the state development authority. The site sits two miles north of Houston. Case ADL 234762.

What the land is for

The plan is a multi-use industrial and energy district, and scalable data centers are named among the uses, per the project decision and local coverage. Data centers are the physical plant of modern AI. Free land is meant to pull them in.

Alaska has 8. / Virginia has 639.

Alaska has 8 data centers, among the fewest of any state. Virginia has 639. The state sees a hole to fill, and cheap public land is one lever it can pull.

Not answering demand. / Building it.

This is build it and they will come, aimed at a public asset. Free land is the subsidy, spent before a single data center exists.

The town next door says no

Houston City Council member Lisa Johansen has proposed banning data centers inside city limits. But the state parcel sits about two miles north of Houston, outside the line a town of a few thousand can draw. The town can zone itself, not the land next door.

The choice was never data centers or nothing.

It is the terms. Free or priced. Who zones it, who profits, and who carries the cost if the servers never come. Right now it is only a boundary on a map, which is what a comment period is for.

It is not decided yet

This is a preliminary decision. Public comment on case ADL 234762 runs through 5:00 p.m. on Wednesday, August 19, 2026. If nothing significant changes, the state can then issue it as the final finding and decision.

Comment before Aug 19

Read case ADL 234762 and tell the state what 31 square miles of public land is worth. That is the one price control left before this goes final. Should the state give public land away to attract data centers, or set a price the town next door helps decide?

## What we verified

- The DNR preliminary decision proposes conveying approximately 19,950 acres of state land in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough. [Alaska DNR Online Public Notices](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224431), primary document, 2026-07-10.
- The proposed conveyance is filed under case number ADL 234762. [Alaska DNR Online Public Notices](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224431), primary document, 2026-07-10.

Dan Sullivan](https://www.sullivan.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/sullivan-secures-56-provisions-historic-26-billion-for-alaska-in-fy-2027-defense-authorization), primary document, 2026-06-23.

# A Better Ear Is Not a Recovery

> Cook Inlet has about 331 belugas left, and AI can finally hear them through the ship noise.

Published 2026-07-21 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-21/

## The story

Now a machine can hear them through the ship noise.

Two gates. One white whale.

NOAA Fisheries, Microsoft AI for Good and Alaska Fish and Game built a deep learning listener in two stages. Stage one flags a sound. Stage two names the species behind it.

Down almost 80 percent.

Cook Inlet's belugas are a genetically distinct population, cut off from every other Alaska stock. They fell from about 1,300 whales in 1979 to 279 by 2018, and were listed endangered in 2008.

A whale in a wall of noise.

Ocean noise is one of the biggest threats NOAA lists for these belugas. In a crowded inlet a single call can vanish under a passing ship. Hearing them at all is the first problem.

It learns the calls it used to miss.

The model uses contrastive audio language models and active learning. It sorts a sound into beluga, killer whale or humpback, flags the calls it is unsure of for a person to label, and firms up a daily read of where belugas are.

Ears below. Eyes above.

A separate NOAA led effort, with the U.S. Geological Survey, Microsoft AI for Good and the Naval Research Laboratory, is teaching a cloud model to spot the same whales in satellite images.

331 today. Still far below 1979.

The machine measures the whale. It cannot move it.

A sharper ear tells managers where and when the belugas are. It does not quiet the ships, refill the prey, or clear the inlet. The hunt has been closed since 2007, and the whales still have not recovered.

A better ear is not a recovery.

AI can finally hear Alaska's most endangered whale. What would it take to bring it back?

## What we verified

- A 2026 study titled "Adaptive Acoustic Monitoring for Endangered Cook Inlet Beluga Whales in Complex Soundscapes" was published in the journal Marine Mammal Science. [Marine Mammal Science (Crossref record)](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1111/mms.70213), report, 2026-06-07.
- The Cook Inlet beluga population declined by nearly 80 percent between 1979 and 2018, from about 1,300 whales to an estimated 279. [NOAA Fisheries](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/species/beluga-whale), report.
- In 2008, the Cook Inlet beluga population was listed as endangered under the Endangered Species Act. [NOAA Fisheries](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/species/beluga-whale), report.
- In 2011, NOAA Fisheries designated two areas of Cook Inlet as critical habitat. [NOAA Fisheries](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/species/beluga-whale), report.
- NOAA Fisheries identifies five beluga whale stocks in Alaskan waters, and the Cook Inlet stock is geographically isolated from the others. [NOAA Fisheries](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/species/beluga-whale), report.
- NOAA lists threats to Cook Inlet belugas including ocean noise, prey limitations, habitat impacts, contaminants, predation, strandings, disease and changing climate conditions. [NOAA Fisheries](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/species/beluga-whale), report.
- Although the subsistence hunt has been suspended since 2007, the Cook Inlet beluga population has not recovered as expected. [NOAA Fisheries](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/species/beluga-whale), report.
- The Cook Inlet beluga whale is managed as a Distinct Population Segment (DPS). [NOAA Fisheries](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/species/beluga-whale), report.
- The paper was published online first on June 7, 2026, with a print issue dated July 2026. [Marine Mammal Science (Crossref record)](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1111/mms.70213), report, 2026-06-07.
- The study was a NOAA Fisheries, Microsoft AI for Good, and Alaska Department of Fish and Game collaboration; authors include Verena Gill (NOAA Fisheries, Anchorage), Manuel Castellote and Rahul Dodhia and Juan M. Lavista Ferres (Microsoft AI for Good Research Lab), and Lori Polasek (Alaska Department of Fish and Game). [Marine Mammal Science (Crossref record)](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1111/mms.70213), report, 2026-06-07.
- The framework is a deep-learning dual-stage model that separates signal detection from species classification. [Marine Mammal Science (Crossref abstract)](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1111/mms.70213), report, 2026-06-07.
- The model expands beyond belugas to a multi-species context that also includes killer whales and humpback whales. [Marine Mammal Science (Crossref abstract)](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1111/mms.70213), report, 2026-06-07.
- Using contrastive audio-language models and active learning, the framework improved detection of rare species occurrences and strengthened confidence in daily beluga presence estimates across Cook Inlet regions. [Marine Mammal Science (Crossref abstract)](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1111/mms.70213), report, 2026-06-07.
- NOAA leads a separate collaborative effort with the U.S. Geological Survey, Microsoft AI for Good, the Naval Research Laboratory and other partners to detect Cook Inlet belugas in satellite imagery. [NOAA Fisheries](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/alaska/science-data/satellite-monitoring-cook-inlet-beluga-whales), report.
- The satellite initiative aims to build a secure cloud-based application that uses machine learning to detect whales and other marine mammals in very high-resolution (VHR) satellite imagery. [NOAA Fisheries](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/alaska/science-data/satellite-monitoring-cook-inlet-beluga-whales), report.
- The best current abundance estimate for the Cook Inlet beluga population is 331 whales, suggesting the population may be stabilizing and possibly increasing. [NOAA Fisheries](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/species/beluga-whale), report.

Slides and the deck PDF are linked from the canonical page.

# Written in Pencil

> A Kenai school district bought an $8,300 AI tool for its classrooms, then started writing the rules to govern it.

Published 2026-07-20 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-20/

## The story

AI is already in class. The rulebook is still in pencil.

An $8,300 tool is on the desk. The policy is a draft.

The tool is paid for. The rulebook is a draft.

Kenai's district has spent $8,300 to date on a three year MagicSchool subscription for students and staff. The policy meant to govern it is still a draft.

Two questions decide it.

Student data is the hard boundary.

Under the proposal, teachers could not feed student data into AI tools the district has not approved. Alaska's vetting rules require FERPA and COPPA, the federal student privacy laws.

Write it in pencil, not ink.

Alaska already has a playbook.

Not whether. How.

The deadline is fall.

Kenai aims to have its AI rules in place by the start of the new school year. Its committee began this work in 2025, building on the state framework.

## What we verified

- The Alaska DEED district guidance lays out a 6-step policy development process. [Alaska DEED](https://education.alaska.gov/artificial-intelligence/district), primary document.
- The DEED guidance urges a balanced, human-centered approach that augments human capabilities without replacing essential judgment or interaction. [Alaska DEED](https://education.alaska.gov/artificial-intelligence/district), primary document.
- The DEED vetting checklist explicitly mandates federal student-privacy compliance (FERPA and COPPA). [Alaska DEED](https://education.alaska.gov/artificial-intelligence/district), primary document.
- The DEED guidance cites that approximately 15% of students are aware of AI-generated explicit images depicting their classmates (a cited rationale for guardrails). [Alaska DEED](https://education.alaska.gov/artificial-intelligence/district), primary document.
- DEED recommends allowing at least 6-8 weeks for a meaningful AI pilot evaluation. [Alaska DEED](https://education.alaska.gov/artificial-intelligence/district), primary document.
- The Kenai Peninsula Borough School District is proposing comprehensive AI policies addressing academic honesty and student data protection. [KBBI/KDLL public radio](https://www.kbbi.org/2026-07-08/proposed-school-district-ai-policies-target-academic-honesty-student-privacy), report, 2026-07-08.
- The Alaska DEED framework centers on seven guiding principles, human-centered design, fair access, transparency, oversight, security, ethical use, and cultural responsiveness. [EdTech Innovation Hub](https://www.edtechinnovationhub.com/news/alaska-becomes-32nd-us-state-to-release-k-12-ai-education-framework), report, 2025-10.
- Alaska districts named as engaged in AI-policy work include Fairbanks, Mat-Su, Wrangell, and Anchorage. [EdTech Innovation Hub](https://www.edtechinnovationhub.com/news/alaska-becomes-32nd-us-state-to-release-k-12-ai-education-framework), report, 2025-10.
- The district has spent $8,300 to date on a three-year MagicSchool subscription for students and staff (an education-specific AI platform). [KBBI/KDLL](https://www.kbbi.org/2026-07-08/proposed-school-district-ai-policies-target-academic-honesty-student-privacy), report, 2026-07-08.
- Under the proposal, teachers would be barred from feeding student data into AI platforms not approved by the district. [KBBI/KDLL](https://www.kbbi.org/2026-07-08/proposed-school-district-ai-policies-target-academic-honesty-student-privacy), report, 2026-07-08.
- The proposed academic-honesty change defines academic honesty, outlines how AI tools can be used responsibly, and sets consequences for inappropriate use like plagiarism. [KBBI/KDLL](https://www.kbbi.org/2026-07-08/proposed-school-district-ai-policies-target-academic-honesty-student-privacy), report, 2026-07-08.
- The district's AI-specific committee was established in 2025 and reviewed Alaska DEED guidelines in fall 2025. [KBBI/KDLL](https://www.kbbi.org/2026-07-08/proposed-school-district-ai-policies-target-academic-honesty-student-privacy), report, 2026-07-08.
- District administrators aim to implement the new AI policies by the beginning of the new school year. [KBBI/KDLL](https://www.kbbi.org/2026-07-08/proposed-school-district-ai-policies-target-academic-honesty-student-privacy), report, 2026-07-08.
- Board member Mica VanBuskirk urged that teachers keep discretion over acceptable AI use case by case. [KBBI/KDLL](https://www.kbbi.org/2026-07-08/proposed-school-district-ai-policies-target-academic-honesty-student-privacy), report, 2026-07-08.
- VanBuskirk framed the urgency of getting AI rules right now. [KBBI/KDLL](https://www.kbbi.org/2026-07-08/proposed-school-district-ai-policies-target-academic-honesty-student-privacy), report, 2026-07-08.
- Assistant Superintendent Kari Dendurent cautioned that overly strict parameters could limit needed flexibility as the policy evolves. [KBBI/KDLL](https://www.kbbi.org/2026-07-08/proposed-school-district-ai-policies-target-academic-honesty-student-privacy), report, 2026-07-08.
- Alaska became the 32nd US state to release a K-12 AI education framework, titled 'Artificial Intelligence for K-12, Recommendations and Considerations for Districts.'. [EdTech Innovation Hub](https://www.edtechinnovationhub.com/news/alaska-becomes-32nd-us-state-to-release-k-12-ai-education-framework), report, 2025-10.

# Reading the Frozen Ground at the Top of America

> Under one road in Utqiagvik, the northernmost US city, two buried cables now teach the frozen ground to forecast its own thaw.

Published 2026-07-19 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-19/

## The story

The frozen ground now forecasts itself

Two buried cables. Three winters of data. One Alaska road.

Two cables. One road. A kilometer each.

Under one road embankment in Utqiagvik, the northernmost city in the United States, a Penn State team buried a pair of fiber-optic cables, each 1 km (0.6 mi) long, to feel the ground.

Warming ground breaks what we build on it

Permafrost worldwide is warming, by up to almost 2 F per decade. If the thaw holds, Arctic communities could see billions in damaged roads, pipes, and buildings. The old answer is to guess. The new one is to measure.

The wire that listens to frost

For 33 months, the cables read temperature and seismic motion straight from the embankment. Terabytes of ground, recorded in the dark.

A live twin, fed by the buried cables

They fused physics equations with machine learning to build a digital twin, a real-time simulation of that embankment, fed by the cables. This is narrow, physics-informed AI, not a general or generative one.

DIGITAL TWIN / UTQIAGVIK EMBANKMENT

Not a smarter guess. A guess the ground corrects.

Each forecast meets the next real reading, and the gap teaches the model. The value is not certainty. It is a prediction the frozen ground itself keeps grading, season after season.

One kilometer, lit. The rest is dark ground.

This models one embankment, not the North Slope. The team says the method is broadly transferable, which is a claim, not a deployment.

Fund a decade more of ground truth?

The lead researcher wants about 10 more years of data, an aspiration, not a funded plan. So the real question for Alaska, keep the wire in the ground, or harden the roads we already know are failing?

## What we verified

- A two-stage deep-learning pipeline pairs a patch-based pretrain classifier with HerdNet point detection to count caribou in gigapixel aerial mosaics. [frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/ecology-and-evolution/articles/10.3389/fevo.2026.1727514/full), report, 2026-02-26.
- The method achieved F1 scores of 95.5% (2017) and 93.3% (2019), beating baseline initialization. [frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/ecology-and-evolution/articles/10.3389/fevo.2026.1727514/full), report, 2026-02-26.
- The study covers five caribou herds distributed across Alaska (Central Arctic, Fortymile, Porcupine, Teshekpuk, Western Arctic). [frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/ecology-and-evolution/articles/10.3389/fevo.2026.1727514/full), report, 2026-02-26.
- Imagery was captured at roughly 2 to 4.3 cm ground-sampling distance from about 450 m altitude during July 2017 and July 2019 surveys. [frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/ecology-and-evolution/articles/10.3389/fevo.2026.1727514/full), report, 2026-02-26.
- The study was published in Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution on February 26, 2026. [frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/ecology-and-evolution/articles/10.3389/fevo.2026.1727514/full), report, 2026-02-26.
- A Penn State-led team buried a pair of 1-kilometer-long fiber-optic cables to collect thermal and seismic data from the ground. [phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-06-digital-twin-alaska-permafrost-real.html), report, 2026-06-16.
- A section of the cables runs along a road embankment in Utqiagvik, Alaska, the northernmost city in the United States. [phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-06-digital-twin-alaska-permafrost-real.html), report, 2026-06-16.
- The cables collected temperature and seismic data from September 2021 to June 2024. [phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-06-digital-twin-alaska-permafrost-real.html), report, 2026-06-16.
- Permafrost worldwide is warming, with ground temperatures increasing by up to almost 2 degrees F per decade (a general statement about global permafrost, not the measured Utqiagvik embankment). [phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-06-digital-twin-alaska-permafrost-real.html), report, 2026-06-16.
- Lead researcher Ming Xiao said about 10 more years of data would be extremely valuable to the broader scientific community. [phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-06-digital-twin-alaska-permafrost-real.html), report, 2026-06-16.
- The work was led by Ming Xiao (professor of civil engineering) and Tieyuan Zhu (associate professor of geosciences), both at Penn State. [phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-06-digital-twin-alaska-permafrost-real.html), report, 2026-06-16.
- The study was published in the Journal of Geophysical Research, Earth Surface in 2026. [phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-06-digital-twin-alaska-permafrost-real.html), report, 2026-06-16.
- The framework is a digital twin, it processes terabytes of data to create a real-time simulation of an area or object. [phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-06-digital-twin-alaska-permafrost-real.html), report, 2026-06-16.
- The method combines physics equations, mathematical functions, and AI-powered machine learning (physics-informed machine learning). [phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-06-digital-twin-alaska-permafrost-real.html), report, 2026-06-16.
- The approach more accurately predicts the embankment permafrost's physical properties, including unfrozen water content, ground temperature, and how heat moves through the ground. [phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-06-digital-twin-alaska-permafrost-real.html), report, 2026-06-16.
- The digital twin simulates one specific road embankment, but the researchers say the idea and process can be broadly transferable to other cold-region infrastructure monitoring. [phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-06-digital-twin-alaska-permafrost-real.html), report, 2026-06-16.
- Arctic communities and governments could see billions of dollars in infrastructure damage over the coming decades if the thawing trend continues. [phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-06-digital-twin-alaska-permafrost-real.html), report, 2026-06-16.
- Alaska DNR proposes to lease a 715.4-acre parcel of North Slope state land (ADL 422741) for a natural-gas-powered high-performance-computing facility. [aws.state.ak.us](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224224), report, 2026-06-17.
- The proposed lease term is 50 years. [aws.state.ak.us](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224224), report, 2026-06-17.
- The public comment deadline was July 17, 2026, at 4:30 PM Alaska Daylight Time. [aws.state.ak.us](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224224), report, 2026-06-17.
- The site is about 26 miles south of Deadhorse and roughly one mile west of the Dalton Highway. [aws.state.ak.us](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224224), report, 2026-06-17.
- DNR received more than 500 public comments, of which fewer than a dozen endorsed the project. [adn.com](https://www.adn.com/business-economy/2026/07/07/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-07.
- The comment period was extended to July 17 due to the volume of comments, public interest, and requests for extension. [adn.com](https://www.adn.com/business-economy/2026/07/07/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-07.
- The campus would include 1 to 3 gigawatts of on-site natural-gas-fired generation. [northern.org](https://northern.org/news/stak-energy-campus-what-the-states-lease-documents-reveal-about-scale-risk-and-unanswered-questions/), report, 2026-05-28.
- The facility would burn roughly 350 to 500 million standard cubic feet of gas per day. [northern.org](https://northern.org/news/stak-energy-campus-what-the-states-lease-documents-reveal-about-scale-risk-and-unanswered-questions/), report, 2026-05-28.
- Construction would require roughly 7.1 million cubic yards of gravel fill. [northern.org](https://northern.org/news/stak-energy-campus-what-the-states-lease-documents-reveal-about-scale-risk-and-unanswered-questions/), report, 2026-05-28.
- Estimated project cost exceeds $10 billion, with roughly $500 million in up-front site development. [adn.com](https://www.adn.com/business-economy/2026/07/07/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-07.

Slides and the deck PDF are linked from the canonical page.

# Alaska data centers and your power bill, on the grid or off

> A data center on the North Slope cannot touch your Anchorage power bill. One in the Mat-Su can.

Published 2026-07-18 by Alaska AI. 9 slides.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/archive/2026-07-18/

## The story

Will a data center raise your power bill?

In Alaska the honest answer splits on one line.

On the grid, or off it.

OFF THE GRID. Runs on its own gas. Never touches your wires. ON THE GRID. Shares the wires, and the bill, with you.

The one everyone feared is off the line.

STAK's proposed campus sits about 25 miles south of Deadhorse and self-generates a gigawatt or more, roughly 30 percent above urban Alaska's peak. It burns gas behind the meter, with no wire to the Railbelt.

This one plugs into your grid.

The state just moved to hand AIDEA about 30 square miles of land near Houston for a data-center district, on the Railbelt. Public comment is open through August 19.

It all turns on the rate deal.

RATES COULD FALL. A big anchor load can spread fixed costs, Launch Alaska argues. RATES COULD RISE. Or compete for scarce Railbelt gas.

The case for lower, in one chart.

And every 1% drop leaves about $2.5M in fixed costs with nowhere to go. A big anchor load could spread those costs, the argument goes. Could.

Alaska is at the very beginning.

Eight data centers here, against the nation's leader at 639, as reported by Alaska's News Source. The rules get written while the count is still small.

Build vs ban is the wrong fight.

Houston is weighing a ban, postponed to August 13. But the lever is the rate deal. Anchorage adopted guardrails 10 to 2. The statewide bill that would set rate rules, HB 259, still sits in the House Energy Committee.

Before the next data center plugs in, ask one thing. Who writes the rate deal, and does it lower your bill or raise it?

On the grid or off it changes everything. What should Alaska require first?

## What we verified

- Alaska's DNR moved to transfer about 30 square miles of state land north of Houston in the Mat-Su to AIDEA for a multi-use industrial and energy development district that includes data centers. [Alaska's News Source](https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/07/17/new-state-proposal-could-bring-data-centers-mat-su-part-industrial-park/), report, 2026-07-17.
- AIDEA Executive Director Randy Ruaro said there are no pre-determined and set land use decisions made by AIDEA. [Alaska Beacon](https://alaskabeacon.com/2026/07/16/alaskas-economic-development-agency-plans-a-mat-su-industrial-park-with-data-centers/), report, 2026-07-16.
- The DNR preliminary decision on the Mat-Su transfer runs 41 pages. [Alaska's News Source](https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/07/17/new-state-proposal-could-bring-data-centers-mat-su-part-industrial-park/), report, 2026-07-17.

[Alaska's News Source](https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/07/17/new-state-proposal-could-bring-data-centers-mat-su-part-industrial-park/), report, 2026-07-17.
- Alaska currently has 8 data centers compared with Virginia's nation-leading 639. [Alaska's News Source](https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/07/17/new-state-proposal-could-bring-data-centers-mat-su-part-industrial-park/), report, 2026-07-17.
- STAK Energy's proposed North Slope AI and cloud campus sits about 25 miles south of Deadhorse just off the Dalton Highway and would self-generate a gigawatt or more of power, roughly 30 percent more than the peak demand of urban Alaska's entire grid. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.

- The STAK campus would consume roughly 350 to 500 million standard cubic feet of North Slope gas per day. [Northern Alaska Environmental Center](https://northern.org/news/stak-energy-campus-what-the-states-lease-documents-reveal-about-scale-risk-and-unanswered-questions/), report, 2026-05-28.

[Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- Because the STAK North Slope project is off-grid and self-generating hundreds of miles from urban Alaska, reporting states its fuel sales would have no direct impact on city dwellers' electricity prices. [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), report, 2026-07-03.
- In an April 2026 ADN opinion piece, Launch Alaska's Penny Gage wrote that Chugach-area electric sales have declined about 1 percent a year for roughly 15 years, dropped another 2.3 percent in 2025, and that every 1 percent reduction leaves about 2.5 million dollars in fixed costs with nowhere to go, arguing a large new anchor load could spread those costs and lower rates. [Anchorage Daily News (opinion)](https://www.adn.com/opinions/2026/04/29/opinion-the-hidden-threat-to-your-electric-bill-and-what-we-can-do-about-it/), report, 2026-04-29.
- The Railbelt already faces a shortage of locally produced gas, which is why adding large new load raises a gas-supply concern rather than a wires concern. [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/alaska-news/anchorage/2026/03/04/data-centers-powering-the-ai-boom-demand-local-energy-anchorage-assembly-members-want-to-regulate-them/), report, 2026-03-04.

[Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/alaska-news/anchorage/2026/03/04/data-centers-powering-the-ai-boom-demand-local-energy-anchorage-assembly-members-want-to-regulate-them/), report, 2026-03-04.
