# AIDEA's free state land for a Mat-Su data center park

> A DNR preliminary decision would transfer about 20,000 acres, roughly 30 square miles, of state land just north of Houston in the Mat-Su to the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority at no charge, a state subsidy meant to seed a multi-use industrial and energy district that includes scalable data centers and a logistics hub about 60 road miles north of Anchorage. Public comment runs through August 19.

Status: open for comment. Decided by Alaska DNR, Commissioner John Crowther.
Public access: open to you. Anyone can comment on the DNR preliminary decision to transfer the land to AIDEA through 5 p.m. August 19, 2026, on the DNR website. Commenting also buys standing, because the notice says only people from whom the division receives timely written comment during this window will be eligible to appeal the Final Finding and Decision. This is the one open comment room among the tracked decisions.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/aidea-houston-industrial-park/

## Dates

- 2026-07-13, Preliminary decision reported (milestone)
- 2026-08-13, Houston City Council vote on a data-center ban ordinance (postponed from July 16) (vote)
- 2026-08-19, Public comment closes (deadline)
- 2026-08-26, AIDEA board meeting, the first after comment closes (milestone)

## Sources

- [Alaska DNR Online Public Notices](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224431), 2026-07-10
- [Reporting From Alaska](https://www.dermotcole.com/reportingfromalaska/2026/7/13/khxwch2o4tgrjxuwycm8kmjzjtp69q), 2026-07-13
- [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/alaskas-economic-development-agency-plans-a-mat-su-industrial-park-with-data-centers/), 2026-07-15
- [Mat-Su Sentinel](https://www.matsusentinel.com/state-agency-plans-houston-area-industrial-park-data-centers-distribution-hub/), 2026-07-14
- [Anchorage Daily News, AIDEA opinion](https://www.adn.com/opinions/2026/08/04/opinion-the-best-time-to-shape-mat-su-development-is-before-it-begins/), 2026-08-04
- [Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority](https://www.aidea.org/About/Board-Members/Board-Meeting-Schedule), 2026-08-06

## How this decision moved

**2026-07-17** Tracked. DNR under Commissioner John Crowther released a 45 page preliminary decision to give about 20,000 acres near Houston to AIDEA at no charge for a data center and industrial district, with public comment open through August 19. Reported by Dermot Cole on July 13 and Northern Journal on July 15.
**2026-07-18** Re-verified against Alaska Beacon and Alaska News Source. The 41 page DNR preliminary decision would transfer about 30 square miles of state land north of Houston to AIDEA at no cost for a multi use industrial and energy development district that includes data centers, with public comment open through 5 p.m. August 19. AIDEA director Randy Ruaro said there are no pre determined and set land use decisions. Houston Council Member Johansen introduced a June ordinance to ban data centers within city limits and the council postponed the vote to August 13. Unlike the off grid North Slope campus, a Railbelt data center here could move household bills either way depending on the utility rate deal.
**2026-07-21** Re-verified against Mat-Su Sentinel and Alaska News Source reporting from July 15 and 16. The City of Houston council took up Council Member Lisa Johansen's ordinance to ban data center development inside city limits and voted July 16 to postpone action to its August 13 meeting, so a small municipality is now moving to zone out the buildout on the state parcel next door on permafrost thaw and water supply grounds. DNR public comment on the no cost land transfer to AIDEA still runs through 5 p.m. August 19. Added the August 13 council vote as a tracked key date.
**2026-07-22** Selected as this run's carousel. Re-verified the DNR primary notice ADL 234762. It remains a preliminary decision proposing a noncompetitive no-cost conveyance of about 19,950 acres of state land roughly two miles north of Houston to AIDEA, with written public comment open through 5 p.m. August 19. The notice says that if no significant change is required the preliminary decision will issue as the Final Finding and Decision. Daniel Jenkins is the listed contact. This is the one open comment room among the tracked decisions.
**2026-07-26** Re-verified against Northern Journal. Public comment on the DNR preliminary decision runs through August 19 and the Houston City Council postponed its vote on a data center restriction ordinance to its next meeting on August 13, to allow a work session that had not yet been scheduled. Parcel described as 30 square miles, roughly 60 road miles north of Anchorage. Dates unchanged.
**2026-07-29** Correction. Between July 21 and today this entry showed August 13 as the comment deadline. That is the date of a separate Houston City Council vote, which stays tracked here as its own key date. The DNR comment deadline was and remains 5 p.m. August 19, 2026, re-verified today against the primary notice, Alaska DNR Online Public Notices id 224431, ADL 234762, which shows no extension or amendment.
**2026-07-31** Re-verified today against the primary notice, Alaska DNR Online Public Notices id 224431. The deadline is unchanged at 5 p.m. Wednesday, August 19, 2026, the parcel is approximately 19,950 acres about two miles north of Houston, and no extension, amendment or correction appears. Two things worth stating plainly for anyone deciding whether to write. First, the notice limits appeal rights to people who comment during this window, so a comment is the only way to keep a say after the decision issues. Second, the Houston City Council vote tracked here for August 13 is a separate question before a separate body. Mat-Su Sentinel reporting places this parcel outside Houston city limits, and the Matanuska-Susitna Borough, which does have jurisdiction, does not require a special permit for a data center, so a city ban would not by itself reach this land.
**2026-08-04** Re-verified against the primary notice. The comment deadline is unchanged at 5:00 p.m. Wednesday, August 19, 2026, Alaska DNR Online Public Notices id 224431, ADL 234762.
**2026-08-05** AIDEA argued its case in the opinion pages. Deputy director Brandon Brefczynski published a piece in the Anchorage Daily News on August 4 stating there is no committed data center tenant, industrial developer, site plan, power source, cooling system, water supply plan or construction schedule, and that what is open through August 19 is the land decision itself. The Houston City Council vote on a data center ban ordinance is still set for August 13.
**2026-08-06** A reader asked for the authority's funding decisions to be tracked more widely. The one that touches this beat is already here, and it now carries the date the board next sits. The authority's published schedule lists a board meeting on Wednesday, August 26th, 2026, which is the first after public comment closes on August 19th, and the schedule notes that its dates are subject to change or cancellation. No agenda for that meeting has been posted, so whether this project is on it is not yet knowable.
**2026-08-07** Re-verified today against the primary notice, Alaska DNR Online Public Notices id 224431. The comment deadline is 5:00 p.m. Wednesday, August 19, 2026 on the proposed noncompetitive conveyance of about 19,950 acres near Houston to AIDEA. No decision has been issued.
**2026-08-08** Re-verified today against the primary notice, Alaska DNR Online Public Notices id 224431, ADL 234762. The notice reads that the deadline for public comment is 5:00 PM, Wednesday, August 19, 2026, and the entry is unchanged. Only people who comment in writing by that time may appeal the final finding and decision. The Houston City Council vote on an ordinance banning data centers inside city limits remains set for August 13.
**2026-08-09** Re-verified today against the primary notice, Alaska DNR Online Public Notices id 224431, ADL 234762. The notice reads that the deadline for public comment is 5:00 PM, Wednesday, August 19, 2026 on the proposed conveyance of about 19,950 acres near Houston to AIDEA, and no Final Finding and Decision has been issued. Only persons from whom the division receives timely written comment during that period will be eligible to appeal. The Houston City Council vote on the ordinance that would ban data centers inside city limits remains set for August 13, 2026, postponed there from July 16.
**2026-08-12** Re-verified against the state notice. Public comment on the roughly 19,950 acre conveyance north of Houston still closes 5 p.m. on August 19th. The Houston City Council's separate vote on a data center ban ordinance remains set for August 13th.
**2026-08-13** Re-verified against the state notice. Public comment on the roughly 19,950 acre conveyance north of Houston, ADL 234762, still closes 5 p.m. on August 19th, and only people who comment in writing during the window can appeal. The Houston City Council's separate vote on a data center ban ordinance is still set for August 13th, postponed there from July 16th.

# The Dixon Glacier diversion into Bradley Lake

> The Alaska Energy Authority has asked FERC to amend the license for the Bradley Lake Hydroelectric Project, the largest in Alaska, so it can build a new dam diverting meltwater and surface runoff from the Dixon Glacier into Bradley Lake, raise the lake's normal maximum operating pool by about 16 feet, and install a 0.3 megawatt micro-hydro turbine in one of the dam's fishwater release valves. The application projects about 38 percent more average annual generation while installed capacity rises from 119.7 to 120.0 megawatts, because the gain comes from water rather than from turbines. AEA estimates construction at about $400 million and about three years of study and permitting followed by three years of construction. FERC accepting the application for filing is a procedural step and not an approval.

Status: open for comment. Decided by Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.
Public access: open to you. Anyone may file a comment, a motion to intervene or a protest with FERC in docket P-8221-124 until 5:00 p.m. Eastern on August 28, which is 1:00 p.m. Alaska time. FERC's eFiling system takes filings online and the notice also gives a mailing address.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/bradley-lake-dixon-diversion/

## Dates

- 2026-06-30, Amendment application filed with FERC (milestone)
- 2026-07-23, AEA board endorses a financing package for the expansion (milestone)
- 2026-08-03, FERC notice published in the Federal Register (milestone)
- 2026-08-28, Comments, motions to intervene and protests due, 5:00 p.m. Eastern (deadline)

## Sources

- [Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, via govinfo.gov](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-08-03/html/2026-15691.htm), 2026-08-03
- [Alaska Energy Authority](https://www.akenergyauthority.org/What-We-Do/Railbelt-Energy/Bradley-Lake-Hydroelectric-Project/Dixon-Diversion-Project), 2026-08-04
- [Alaska Energy Authority](https://www.akenergyauthority.org/What-We-Do/Railbelt-Energy/Bradley-Lake-Hydroelectric-Project), 2026-08-04
- [Petroleum News](https://www.petroleumnews.com/story/2026/08/02/news/aea-final-amendment-application-for-bradley-lake-filed-with-ferc/50288.html), 2026-08-02

## How this decision moved

**2026-08-04** Tracked. FERC accepted the amendment application for filing and opened a comment window closing 5:00 p.m. Eastern on August 28. The project details, the capacity figures and the 38 percent generation projection were read from the Federal Register notice. The cost estimate, the schedule and the siting 27 miles northeast of Homer come from AEA's own project page. Bradley Lake supplies about 10 percent of the power Railbelt utilities use each year.
**2026-08-07** Re-verified today against the Federal Register notice and the Alaska Energy Authority's project page. The comment window is open and closes at 5:00 p.m. Eastern on August 28th. The June 30th final amendment application, the roughly $400 million estimate and the three years of study and permitting followed by three years of construction all stand.
**2026-08-12** Re-verified against the FERC notice. Comments, motions to intervene and protests are still due 5 p.m. Eastern on August 28th in docket P-8221-124. The amendment would raise the lake about 16 feet, add a 0.3 megawatt micro-hydro turbine, and take the project from 119.7 to 120.0 megawatts while adding roughly 38 percent to average annual generation.

# STAK Energy's North Slope AI campus lease

> A preliminary decision would give STAK Energy a 50-year lease on 715.4 acres of state land about 26 miles south of Deadhorse for a gas-fired AI and cloud campus its developer pegs at more than $10 billion, with 1 to 3 gigawatts of on-site generation. More than 500 public comments arrived before the first deadline; fewer than a dozen supported the project.

Status: pending decision. Decided by Alaska DNR, Division of Oil and Gas.
Public access: closed. The written comment window closed 4:30 p.m. July 17, 2026. DNR now weighs more than 500 comments before a final best-interest decision on the 50-year lease. No public comment path remains open.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/adl-422741-stak-north-slope-lease/

## Dates

- 2026-05-12, Preliminary decision noticed (ADL 422741) (milestone)
- 2026-06-15, Original comment deadline (milestone)
- 2026-06-17, Comment period extended for volume and public interest (milestone)
- 2026-07-17, Public comment closes, 4:30 p.m. AKDT (deadline)

## Sources

- [Alaska DNR Online Public Notices](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224224), 2026-06-17
- [Alaska DNR Online Public Notices](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=223817), 2026-05-12
- [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), 2026-07-03
- [Northern Journal](https://www.northernjournal.com/data-center-critics-flood-alaska-land-managers-with-opposition-to-north-slope-project/), 2026-07-06

## How this decision moved

**2026-07-08** Tracked. 500 plus comments on record, fewer than a dozen in favor; deadline already extended once.
**2026-07-09** Re-verified via Northern Journal and ADN. More than 500 comments on record, fewer than a dozen in favor. DNR spokesperson Sean Clifton attributes the extension to comment volume, public interest and requests for extension. Stak's John Boyle calls most comments form letters lacking substance. Comment window stays open to July 17.
**2026-07-10** Re-confirmed via Northern Journal. The comment window still closes July 17, still more than 500 comments with fewer than a dozen in support. No change to the schedule. One week out.
**2026-07-11** Re-confirmed via Northern Journal (July 3 reporting) during this run's fact-check. Comment window still closes 4:30 p.m. July 17, still more than 500 comments with fewer than a dozen in support. Six days out.
**2026-07-12** By early July more than 500 public comments had reached DNR on the North Slope lease, with fewer than a dozen in favor, and the comment deadline held at July 17. Opposition ranged across Kodiak, Kotzebue, Seward, Valdez and Nuiqsut and mixed subsistence, tundra gravel and climate objections with a widely repeated but factually shaky fear of higher power bills, since the North Slope is not tied to the Railbelt grid.
**2026-07-14** Three days out. The written comment window on ADL 422741 still closes at 4:30 p.m. July 17 per DNR reporting, still more than 500 comments on record with fewer than a dozen in support. No schedule change surfaced this run. This is the one open-comment room among the tracked decisions.
**2026-07-15** Two days out. Re-confirmed against Anchorage Daily News reporting from July 7 that more than 500 public comments oppose the Stak Energy North Slope data center lease and fewer than a dozen endorse it, with the written comment window still closing 4:30 p.m. July 17. No schedule change surfaced. This remains the one open comment room among the tracked decisions.
**2026-07-17** Comment day. The written comment window on ADL 422741 closes at 4:30 p.m. today, the one open comment room among the tracked decisions. After it closes the lease moves to a pending final decision by DNR. More than 500 comments on record with fewer than a dozen in support, unchanged this run.
**2026-07-18** The written comment window closed at 4:30 p.m. July 17, so the lease moves to a pending final decision by DNR Division of Oil and Gas. More than 500 comments on record with fewer than a dozen in support. Reporting notes the campus is off-grid and self-generating on North Slope gas hundreds of miles from urban Alaska, so its fuel use would not directly raise Railbelt household electricity prices. This run reframed the docket around that on-grid versus off-grid distinction.
**2026-07-19** Re-verified the DNR primary notice this run. ADL 422741 remains a preliminary decision with no Final Finding and Decision issued yet. The written comment window closed 4:30 p.m. July 17, so the 50-year lease now sits with DNR Division of Oil and Gas for a final best-interest decision. More than 500 comments on record with fewer than a dozen in support, unchanged.
**2026-07-20** Re-verified via Northern Journal. The extended written comment window closed July 17 with more than 500 comments on record and fewer than a dozen in support, and DNR will assess the comments before a final decision on the 50-year lease. No Final Finding and Decision is posted yet.
**2026-07-21** Carried forward against Alaska Beacon and DataCenterDynamics reporting. The written comment window on ADL 422741 closed 4:30 p.m. July 17 with more than 500 comments on record and fewer than a dozen in favor, and the roughly one square mile campus (up to 3 GW, an estimated 350 to 500 million cubic feet of gas per day) now sits with the DNR Division of Oil and Gas for a Final Finding and Decision. No decision is posted yet this run.
**2026-07-22** Re-verified the DNR primary notice ADL 422741. It remains a preliminary decision with no Final Finding and Decision posted. The written comment window closed 4:30 p.m. July 17, so the 50 year lease now sits with DNR Division of Oil and Gas for a final best interest decision. More than 500 comments on record with fewer than a dozen in support, unchanged this run.
**2026-07-24** Selected as this run's carousel. Re-verified the DNR primary notice ADL 422741 with Northern Journal and ADN during this run's fact-check. It remains a preliminary decision with no Final Finding and Decision posted. The written comment window closed 4:30 p.m. July 17, so the 50-year lease now sits with DNR Division of Oil and Gas for a final best-interest decision. More than 500 comments on record with fewer than a dozen in support, unchanged this run. The deck frames the public revolt and the narrow path that remains once the comment room has closed.

**2026-08-12** Re-verified against the state notice. No final best interest decision has been issued on the 715.4 acre, 50-year lease offer, twenty-six days after comment closed.

# Air Force land leases for AI data centers at JBER, Eielson and Clear

> The Air Force offered about 4,700 acres across 12 parcels at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Eielson AFB and Clear Space Force Station for privately financed AI data centers. Residents near the five Eielson-area parcels raised noise, permafrost and grid concerns, including one parcel less than a mile from North Pole Middle School.

Status: pending decision. Decided by Department of the Air Force, Enhanced Use Lease program.
Public access: closed. Proposals closed June 29 and are evaluated privately. No public comment period exists; no award timeline has been announced.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/air-force-eul-ai-data-centers/

## Dates

- 2026-04-10, Program announced (milestone)
- 2026-06-05, Request for lease proposals released (milestone)
- 2026-06-29, Developer proposals due (deadline)
- 2026-07-14, Solicitation AFCEC-26-R-0006 archived with no award posted (milestone)
- 2026-07-22, U.S. House passes FY2027 NDAA carrying a data center lease restriction (vote)
- 2026-07-23, Bill introduced in the U.S. House to ban AI data centers on federal land (milestone)
- 2026-08-10, Proposals due on a separate Eielson mixed-use lease covering 3,967 acres (milestone)

## Sources

- [U.S. Air Force](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/4456660/daf-takes-steps-for-potential-alaskan-ai-data-centers/), 2026-04-10

- [HigherGov (SAM.gov mirror)](https://www.highergov.com/contract-opportunity/rflp-artificial-intelligence-ai-data-center-deve-afcec-26-r-0006-o-db695/), 2026-07-14

## How this decision moved

**2026-07-08** Tracked. Bids closed June 29; no public word yet on how many proposals arrived.
**2026-07-12** Developer lease proposals closed June 29 and the Air Force is now in private evaluation of bids for up to 12 parcels across JBER, Eielson and Clear. The FY2027 NDAA reported by the Senate Armed Services Committee on June 23 would require a formal grid-impact assessment before the military can approve a data-center Enhanced Use Lease, a statutory check Interior utilities and ratepayers had sought.
**2026-07-17** Lease proposals were due June 29 and no developer selection or award has been made public as of this run. Carried forward as pending.
**2026-07-21** A July 19 industry analysis (AIX Energy) notes the Alaska Enhanced Use Lease solicitation for commercial AI data centers on about 4,700 acres across 12 parcels at JBER, Eielson and Clear has moved out of its open proposal phase with no developer award announced, and that unlike the Lower 48 portfolio (which set 100 MW and 500 million dollar minimums) the Alaska request's specific megawatt and capital thresholds are not disclosed. Carried forward as pending decision.
**2026-07-25** Re-verified by fetching the solicitation record for AFCEC-26-R-0006. The response deadline was June 29, 2026 at 5 p.m. EDT, extended from May 29, and the opportunity now reads Past Due with no award and no awardee recorded, last updated July 14, 2026. Twenty-six days past the deadline the three Alaska installations named in the request, JBER, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station, still have no publicly announced lessee. Evaluation is private, so there is no public comment room here.
**2026-07-29** Material update from Congress, verified against primary records. On July 22 at 4:37 p.m. the U.S. House passed H.R. 8800, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, by 216 yea to 212 nay with 3 not voting, and Alaska Representative Nick Begich voted yea, per the House Clerk's roll call 278. Federal News Network reported that the House Armed Services chairman's mark carries an amendment from Rep. Cory Mills of Florida that bars the Defense Department from leasing its land to private companies to build data centers unless they agree not to install or operate data facility equipment containing components manufactured in China, Russia, Iran or North Korea. Army officials warned the standard would drive world class commercial partners and more than 1.3 billion dollars in private capital away from Army land. If it survives conference it narrows who can bid on the Alaska parcels. The Senate has not passed its version. The underlying offer is unchanged, about 4,700 acres across twelve parcels at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station under the enhanced use lease model, which the Air Force says returns at least fair market value in cash.
**2026-07-30** Rep. Rashida Tlaib introduced the No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act on July 23 with five cosponsors. It would permanently ban large AI data centers and associated infrastructure on land owned or managed by the United States, including military bases, and would require existing qualifying facilities to be removed and their sites remediated. The 4,700 acres offered here sit on exactly that kind of land. No award has been announced for the Alaska proposals, which were due June 29. Separately, the Air Force posted a second Eielson land solicitation on July 23 with an August 10 deadline, but that one is for mixed use development and is not part of this offering.
**2026-07-31** Re-checked the solicitation record for AFCEC-26-R-0006. It still reads Past Due with no award and no awardee, thirty-two days after the June 29 proposal deadline. The three Alaska installations named in the request still have no publicly announced lessee. Evaluation is private, so no public comment room exists here.
**2026-08-01** Re-verified today against the Air Force's own announcement, which states approximately 4,700 acres across twelve parcels at Joint Base Elmendorf Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station. That announcement sets no lease term in years, so the fifty year figure that has circulated elsewhere does not come from it. No developer selection has been made public as of this run.
**2026-08-02** A second and separate Eielson solicitation is now open. Request for Lease Proposal AFCEC-26-R-0009 covers four sites totalling 3,967 acres, held a virtual industry day on July 22, and takes proposals until August 10. The Air Force announcement describes it only as mixed-use development, listing residential, commercial, office, cultural, institutional and entertainment uses, and does not mention artificial intelligence or data centers. That is a description of the announcement. The lease document itself is posted on SAM.gov and has not been read here.
**2026-08-03** Still no selection announced. Lease proposals closed June 29, 2026 after an extension from May 29, and five weeks later there is no public award, shortlist or cancellation. Checked today against the Air Force announcement of the offer and the solicitation record for AFCEC-26-R-0006. The offer covers about 4,700 acres across twelve parcels at three installations on ground leases of up to fifty years, so a decision made quietly is a decision with a fifty-year tail.
**2026-08-04** Re-checked. The solicitation for AI data center development on the three installations closed to proposals on June 29 and was archived on July 14 with no award posted. The Air Force's own announcement describes approximately 4,700 acres across twelve parcels and quotes Deputy Assistant Secretary Robert Moriarty saying the offer supports the growing demands of the AI industry. Neither that announcement nor the solicitation record states how much electricity a project would draw.
**2026-08-06** The lease offer says the JBER sites do not have enough power. The Anchorage Daily News, reporting on the solicitation on May 5, 2026, quotes it describing those sites as having insufficient power for a data center and as requiring a new connection to Chugach Electric Association in Anchorage. Chugach's gas supply contract with Hilcorp Alaska, its primary supplier, ends in 2028.
**2026-08-07** Checked and unchanged. No award has been posted on the enhanced use lease covering the three installations. The separate Eielson mixed-use lease still shows proposals due August 10th.
**2026-08-08** Checked and unchanged. Re-verified against the Department of the Air Force announcement of April 10, 2026, which offers approximately 4,700 acres across twelve parcels at the three installations under the enhanced use lease model, with the service receiving at least fair market value in cash. No award and no developer selection has been announced, and the effort remains in solicitation.
**2026-08-09** Checked and unchanged. No award notice has appeared on the request for lease proposals covering about 4,700 acres at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Eielson and Clear, and the Air Force has still announced no award timeline. Proposals closed June 29 and are evaluated privately, so there is no public step for a reader between now and whatever the Air Force announces. The separate Eielson mixed-use lease covering 3,967 acres reaches its proposal deadline August 10, 2026.
**2026-08-13** Checked and unchanged. The federal record for solicitation AFCEC-26-R-0006 still shows the request for lease proposals past due and archived on July 14th, with no award posted and no award timeline announced. Proposals closed June 29th.

# The AKLNG gas line tax bill

> A conference committee compromise unveiled July 2 would swap the state property tax on the Glenfarne-led Alaska LNG project for a volumetric tax after five years of operation or 500 MMcf per day, and extend the completion deadline to the end of 2034. The House deadlocked 19 to 19 on July 16 over an expanded S corporation income tax, the governor rejected that provision, and a third special session convened July 27 with no bill from the governor and almost no legislators in the room.

Status: pending decision. Decided by Alaska Legislature, third special session.
Public access: indirect. Legislators decide; constituents reach them directly. The gas line would feed the grid most Alaska compute would ride on.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/aklng-tax-bill-second-special-session/

## Dates

- 2026-07-02, Draft compromise unveiled (milestone)
- 2026-07-16, Tentative House and Senate floor votes (vote)
- 2026-07-19, Special session ends (milestone)
- 2026-07-27, Third special session convenes, 10:00 a.m. (milestone)
- 2026-08-10, Senate could convene in full if the House passes a bill (milestone)
- 2026-08-12, House Bipartisan Majority Caucus says HB 4001 lacks the votes to pass (milestone)
- 2026-08-20, Joint Senate and House Resources Committee meeting in Anchorage on Cook Inlet energy (milestone)
- 2026-08-25, Third special session scheduled to end (milestone)

## How this decision moved

**2026-07-11** Floor votes still tentatively July 16, session ends July 19, per prior reporting. Alaska Beacon returned HTTP 403 on re-fetch this run; status carried forward unchanged. Watching for the vote.
**2026-07-12** Conferees unveiled a draft compromise on July 2 and set a floor vote for July 16, with the second special session ending July 19. Glenfarne owns 75 percent of the project. The sticking point is an S corporation corporate income tax provision that Governor Dunleavy has vowed to veto, and it is unclear the provision has the House votes. The draft also bars the developer from billing the state if the project is abandoned and requires return of shares and assets within six months.
**2026-07-14** Two days out. **2026-07-17** Update. A conference committee passed the final draft of the gasline tax bill HB 381 on July 16, but Governor Dunleavy rejected the expanded corporate tax and called a third Alaska LNG special session rather than accept it, so the tax terms stay unsettled. A final investment decision still waits on both the tax law and RCA review of the Enstar gas supply agreement.
**2026-07-18** On July 16 the House deadlocked 19 to 19 and the Senate passed the gas-line tax bill 11 to 8 with a 9.4 percent pass-through tax on S corp oil and gas entities. Governor Dunleavy rejected that tax and called a third Alaska LNG special session to convene July 27 in Juneau, so the pipeline tax terms stay unsettled. The AI and data-center link here is indirect, the administration has courted large gas demand to help justify the line.

On July 16 the House deadlocked 19 to 19 and the Senate passed the bill 11 to 8 with a 9.4 percent pass-through tax on S corp oil and gas entities, which Governor Dunleavy rejected. He called a third special session to convene July 27 in Juneau, so the pipeline tax terms stay unsettled and the AI and data-center link stays indirect.
**2026-07-21** Six days out from the third special session, which convenes July 27 in Juneau. Per Anchorage Daily News and Alaska Public Media reporting from July 16 and July 20 the up to 55 billion dollar, 800 mile gas line tax terms remain unsettled after the July 16 House deadlock, with some legislators blaming Hilcorp for the bill's collapse and the governor rejecting that claim. The tie to AI compute stays indirect, the administration has courted large gas demand, including proposed data centers, to help justify the line.
**2026-07-23** Four days out from the third special session, which convenes July 27 in Juneau. The session opens about three weeks before the August 18 primary, per Alaska's News Source and Alaska Public Media reporting from July 16 and July 21. The tie to AI compute stays indirect, the administration has courted large gas demand, including proposed data centers, to justify the roughly 55 billion dollar, 800 mile line.

The tie to AI compute stays indirect, the administration has courted large gas demand, including proposed data centers, to justify the roughly 55 billion dollar, 800 mile line.
**2026-07-25** Two days out from the third special session, which convenes July 27 in Juneau. Re-verified this run by fetching the Alaska Public Media report of July 16. That session opens just over three weeks before the August 18 primary, which is the practical squeeze on it. The tie to AI compute stays indirect, the administration has courted large gas demand, including proposed data centers, to justify the line.

The tie to AI compute stays indirect, the administration has courted large gas demand, including proposed data centers, to justify the line.
**2026-07-30** The third special session opened July 27 as a technical session with three House members and one senator in the room. The governor had not introduced a bill and said his administration would keep meeting with all parties before proposing one. Nothing has moved since.
**2026-08-01** The third special session convened July 27 with four legislators in the room and no bill from the governor. It is scheduled to end August 25. The Senate plans technical sessions until August 10, when it could convene in full if the House passes a bill the governor will accept.
**2026-08-03** The third special session convened Monday, July 27, 2026 with four legislators attending the pro forma opening and no bill from the governor, who said he would work toward a bill acceptable to both the Legislature and Glenfarne. Attendance on the opening day was reported as a handful of members. The scheduled end date of August 25 is unchanged.

**2026-08-08** Re-verified against Alaska's News Source, August 6, 2026. House Speaker Bryce Edgmon and Senate Majority Leader Cathy Giessel also said they had seen no bill. Nothing newer has been published.
**2026-08-13** The bill collapsed. On August 12th the House Bipartisan Majority Caucus said HB 4001 does not appear to have the support needed to pass the Alaska House, with opposition from both majority and minority members, and the Senate Bipartisan Majority Caucus said it does not plan to reconvene. Governor Dunleavy had asked lawmakers to return to Juneau on August 20th. Senate Majority Leader Cathy Giessel said getting 11 senators and 21 representatives to Juneau right now would be a challenge. A joint Senate and House Resources Committee meeting on Cook Inlet energy is planned for August 20th in Anchorage instead.

# Alaska's statewide speech-to-text contract

> Alaska is soliciting one statewide contract to convert speech, live or recorded, into written text for general, medical and legal records. The notice says every state governmental entity may use the resulting contract, naming the Legislative Branch, the Court System, the University of Alaska, boards and commissions, cities, boroughs, school districts and federally recognized tribes. The public notice does not use the terms artificial intelligence, machine learning or automated speech recognition.

Status: pending decision. Decided by Alaska Department of Administration, Office of Procurement and Property Management.
Public access: closed. A vendor solicitation, not a rulemaking, so no public comment period exists. Proposals are evaluated privately. The notice and the named procurement officer are public.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/alaska-statewide-transcription-rfp/

## Dates

- 2026-07-31, Solicitation published on the state public notice system (milestone)
- 2026-08-24, Vendor proposals due, 9:30 a.m. (milestone)

## Sources

- [Alaska Online Public Notice System](https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=224684), 2026-07-31

## How this decision moved

**2026-08-02** Tracked. RFP 2026-0200-0064, published July 31, proposals due August 24. Procurement officer Joshua Hartman. The reach clause and the absence of any technology term were read directly from the published notice.
**2026-08-07** Re-verified today against the state public notice, id 224684. Proposals on RFP 2026-0200-0064 are due at 9:30 a.m. Alaska Daylight Time on Monday, August 24, 2026. No amendment, extension or award has been posted.
**2026-08-12** Re-verified against the state notice. Proposals for RFP 2026-0200-0064 are still due 9:30 a.m. Alaska Daylight Time on August 24th, with no addenda posted.

# A national AI institute for Native communities, and the Alaska lane that closed with it

> The Administration for Native Americans published its final Fiscal Year 2026 program policies on July 28, 2026, standing up three funding opportunities and leaving out SEDS-AK, the Alaska-specific economic development program that ran alongside SEDS for decades. Two days later it posted the AI3 Action Institute, a single national award of up to $3,500,000 to build an artificial intelligence resource center for Native communities, with Alaska Native villages under ANCSA and nonprofit village consortia named as eligible applicants.

Status: pending decision. Decided by Administration for Native Americans, HHS Administration for Children and Families.
Public access: indirect. Only eligible applicants reach this one, so an Alaskan reaches it through a tribe, an ANCSA village or a Native nonprofit that files by August 27. Applications are evaluated privately and no public comment path remains open.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/ana-ai3-action-institute/

## Dates

- 2026-07-28, Final Fiscal Year 2026 issuance published at 91 FR 47241, standing up EAGLE, the AI3 Action Institute and NCNTTA (milestone)

# Alaska's bid to run its own carbon storage permits

> The Alaska Oil and Gas Conservation Commission is applying to the Environmental Protection Agency for primary enforcement authority over Class VI wells, the wells used to inject carbon dioxide for permanent underground storage. If the application succeeds the state, not the federal government, would permit and police every carbon storage well in Alaska.

Status: pending decision. Decided by Alaska Oil and Gas Conservation Commission applies; the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency decides.
Public access: closed. The state comment window closed at the end of the May 14th, 2026 hearing. The federal review of the application carries its own comment period, which has not opened.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/aogcc-class-vi-carbon-storage/

## Dates

- 2026-03-03, Public meeting on adopting the state regulations (milestone)
- 2026-05-14, State hearing, and the close of written and oral comment (deadline)

## Sources

- [Alaska Oil and Gas Conservation Commission](https://www.commerce.alaska.gov/web/aogcc/ccus/Home.aspx), 2026-08-06
- [Petroleum News](https://www.petroleumnews.com/story/2026/04/19/government/aogcc-class-vi-primacy-hearing-scheduled/50086.html), 2026-04-19
- [State of Alaska, draft primacy application](https://www.commerce.alaska.gov/web/Portals/18/pub/Events/Public%20Hearings/2026/2026-05-14/Alaska%20Class%20VI%20UIC%20Primacy%20Application.pdf), 2026-04-09

## How this decision moved

**2026-08-06** Tracked after a reader asked for the carbon capture approval process. The authority comes from two acts of the legislature, chapter 2 of the 2023 session laws directing the commission to seek this authority and chapter 23 of the 2024 session laws establishing the state carbon storage program. The commission held a public meeting on adopting its regulations on March 3rd, 2026 and a hearing on the application itself on May 14th, 2026, with comment closing at the end of that hearing. The commission has said it aims to complete the process in about two years, which other states' experience suggests is optimistic. This matters to the AI build out because the coal plant proposed in the Susitna watershed, tracked separately here, plans to inject its carbon dioxide into a depleted Cook Inlet gas reservoir, and these are the permits that would govern it.

# The Army's Janus microreactor program at Fort Wainwright

> The Army named Fort Wainwright in Fairbanks as one of nine installations that could host a microreactor under its Janus program. Fort Wainwright once exported power from an on site coal plant and is now a net importer, in a region with high energy costs and little spare generation.

Status: pending decision. Decided by Department of the Army, running its solicitation through the Defense Innovation Unit.
Public access: closed. Industry submissions were taken through the Defense Innovation Unit and are evaluated privately. No public comment period exists at this stage, and no vendor has been named for Fort Wainwright.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/army-janus-fort-wainwright/

## Dates

- 2025-11-18, Army solicitation released through the Defense Innovation Unit (milestone)
- 2025-12-15, Industry submissions due (deadline)

## Sources

- [American Nuclear Society, Nuclear Newswire](https://www.ans.org/news/article-7567/us-army-chooses-nine-sites-for-possible-microreactor-by-2030/), 2025-11-20
- [World Nuclear News](https://www.world-nuclear-news.org/articles/us-army-names-potential-microreactor-sites), 2025-11-19

## How this decision moved

**2026-08-06** Tracked. Fort Wainwright is one of nine sites the Army named, alongside Fort Benning, Fort Bragg, Fort Campbell, Fort Drum, Fort Hood, Holston Army Ammunition Plant, Joint Base Lewis McChord and Redstone Arsenal. The Army says the sites were chosen on mission criticality, existing energy shortfalls, grid resilience and environmental and technical constraints. The program answers Executive Order 14299 on deploying advanced nuclear reactor technologies for national security, and the Army's stated goal is an operational demonstration plant on a military installation by 2030. No vendor selection for Fort Wainwright has been made public.

# The Air Force nuclear microreactor at Eielson

> The Air Force intends to award Oklo a 30 year fixed price power purchase agreement for a microreactor delivering up to 5 megawatts to Eielson Air Force Base outside Fairbanks. Oklo would build, own and operate it, and the contract is signed only after Oklo obtains a license from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

Status: pending decision. Decided by Department of the Air Force with Defense Logistics Agency Energy, and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission for the license.
Public access: closed. Contract negotiation is private and the Air Force runs no comment period. The reactor can't be built without a Nuclear Regulatory Commission license, and that review is the room where the public gets a formal say.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/eielson-oklo-microreactor/

## Dates

- 2025-06-11, Air Force announces a notice of intent to award to Oklo (milestone)

## Sources

- [U.S. Air Force](https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/4213048/microreactor-pilot-reaches-major-project-milestone/), 2025-06-11
- [Eielson Air Force Base](https://www.eielson.af.mil/microreactor/), 2026-08-06
- [American Nuclear Society, Nuclear Newswire](https://www.ans.org/news/2025-06-16/article-7114/air-force-issues-notice-to-partner-with-oklo-on-microreactor-deployment-in-alaska/), 2025-06-16
- [Air and Space Forces Magazine](https://www.airandspaceforces.com/air-force-microreactor-eielson-alaska/), 2025-06-12

## How this decision moved

**2026-08-06** Tracked after a reader asked for it, and the reader's own figure did not survive the check. The Air Force program page for the pilot states the capacity, the 30 year power purchase agreement and the licensing condition, and it states no operational date at all. A December 31st, 2027 goal has circulated widely; that comes from the fiscal 2019 defense authorization, which directed that a licensed microreactor be operating on a Defense Department installation by 2027, and it is a statutory goal for the program rather than a commitment for this reactor. A deputy assistant secretary of the Air Force was separately reported hoping the reactor would run by 2030. So the honest position is that no operational date is published, and this entry will not carry one until the Air Force sets one. The notice of intent to award reinstated Oklo after an earlier award was rescinded following a bid protest.
**2026-08-12** Re-verified against the base's own program page. No contract has been awarded. The notice of intent to award opened negotiation with Oklo and the award still waits on the company finishing Nuclear Regulatory Commission licensing. The pilot is sized at up to 5 megawatts for critical infrastructure on the base, under a 30-year power purchase agreement.

# Enstar's Cook Inlet gas storage plan (Kenai Loop Pool)

> On July 10, 2026 the Anchorage Daily News reported the RCA issued a 17-page order denying Enstar's request for an advance determination that its proposed Cook Inlet gas storage project was prudent, saying the utility lacked basic information. The $240 million project would have bought the depleted Kenai Loop Pool reservoir from AIX Energy to hold 25 billion cubic feet of gas, close to half Enstar's annual demand, adding up to $12 a month to the average bill. Enstar and Hilcorp have competing DNR lease applications for the same pool, and DNR has not confirmed it is technically capable of storing gas. Without approval, Enstar president John Sims said the company suspended the project. Enstar reopened the question on July 23, 2026 with a 31-page petition for reconsideration, arguing the order was erroneous and suffers from a lack of true understanding of the nature of the problem, and calling the Kenai Loop Pool the only viable commercial storage option in Cook Inlet. Alaska Public Media reports the commission has thirty days to respond and that inaction is an automatic denial.

Status: pending decision. Decided by Regulatory Commission of Alaska (prudency); Alaska DNR (storage lease and technical determination).
Public access: indirect. The RCA is a governor-appointed, legislature-confirmed commission, and the public reaches its dockets through formal comment and intervention. The prudency question is open again on Enstar's petition for reconsideration. The underlying DNR storage-lease question is also still open.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/enstar-cook-inlet-gas-storage/

## Dates

- 2026-07-10, RCA denies Enstar advance determination of prudency (ADN report); Enstar suspends the project (decision)
- 2026-07-10, DNR determination on Kenai Loop Pool storage capability and competing Enstar/Hilcorp leases still pending (milestone)
- 2026-08-22, RCA acts on Enstar's petition for reconsideration, or the petition is denied automatically (decision)

## Sources

- [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/business-economy/energy/2026/07/10/state-regulators-reject-enstar-gas-storage-plan-raising-questions-about-solution-to-cook-inlet-shortage/), 2026-07-10
- [Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/economy/2026-07-24/enstar-appeals-rca-decision-saying-natural-gas-storage-cant-wait), 2026-07-24
- [Regulatory Commission of Alaska](https://rca.alaska.gov/RCAWeb/ViewFile.aspx?id=b66270b8-2f44-4854-80b3-29bc451a419b), 2026-07-08
- [Alaska's News Source](https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/07/14/alaska-regulators-deny-enstars-request-advance-approval-kenai-gas-storage-project/), 2026-07-13
- [Petroleum News](https://www.petroleumnews.com/story/2026/07/19/utilities/enstar-request-rejected/50264.html), 2026-07-19
- [Petroleum News](https://www.petroleumnews.com/story/2026/08/02/utilities/a-need-for-gas-storage/50284.html), 2026-08-02

## How this decision moved

**2026-07-11** Tracked from this run's verified claims. RCA denied Enstar's advance prudency determination in a 17-page order (ADN, July 10); Enstar suspended the $240M Kenai Loop Pool storage project. The storage fix for Southcentral's Cook Inlet gas crunch is off the table for now; DNR technical/lease determination and the competing Hilcorp application remain unresolved.
**2026-08-03** Reopened. Enstar filed a 31-page petition for reconsideration on July 24, 2026, calling the denial erroneous and the Kenai Loop Pool the only viable commercial storage option in Cook Inlet. The commission has thirty days to respond and inaction denies the petition automatically, which puts the next decision point on or about August 23, 2026, thirty days from the filing. Status moves back from decided to pending. Re-verified today against Alaska Public Media, July 24, 2026.
**2026-08-04** Re-verified against Petroleum News, August 2, 2026, and against the commission's July 8, 2026 order, which Alaska's News Source published in full. The petition for reconsideration was filed July 23, 2026, not July 24 as this entry recorded, which puts the thirty day mark on or about August 22, 2026. The order called an advance determination of prudence an extraordinary request not explicitly contemplated in the commission's governing statutes or regulations, and found the record lacked a sufficient factual basis to judge the $240 million investment prudent. Enstar disputes the finding that a DNR pore space lease approval must come first, and says that starting in 2027 it anticipates a surplus when gas supply purchases will exceed customer demand.
**2026-08-08** Checked and unchanged. No commission order on Enstar's petition for reconsideration has been published. The 31-page petition, filed July 24, 2026, calls the denial erroneous and describes the Kenai Loop Pool as the only viable commercial storage option in Cook Inlet, at an estimated $240 million against more than 150,000 Southcentral customers. Thirty days from filing keeps the next decision point on or about August 22.

# GVEA's $120 million turbine decision

> GVEA's board weighs buying a GE LM6000 combined-cycle turbine, roughly $120 million for 45 to 58 MW, while data center demand has pushed gas turbine plant costs up 195 percent since 2019 and order waitlists into the early 2030s, per a Bloomberg report cited by the News-Miner. The board reserved an order slot in April for $50,000.

Status: pending decision. Decided by Golden Valley Electric Association board of directors.
Public access: indirect. A member-owned co-op board decides, in executive session. GVEA members reach it through board elections and member comment periods at regular meetings.

# The Kenai Peninsula school district's AI rulebook

> The Kenai Peninsula Borough School District is writing the rules for artificial intelligence in its 39 schools while the school year starts. Its Policy Review Committee took up AR 5131.9 Academic Honesty, a new administrative regulation the district says was brought forward in relation to the inclusion of AI, on August 3, 2026, with two competing drafts posted, one from Administration and one from board member Mica VanBuskirk. That same evening the full board took first readings on three more documents the district describes as revised for AI-related policy shifts, AR 5125 Student Records, BP 1114 Communication Using Electronic Media and BP 5131.9 Academic Honesty, plus AR 6161.4 Acceptable Use. Nothing in the package is adopted. The district told KBBI in July that it has spent 8,300 dollars to date on a three year MagicSchool subscription for students and staff, so the classroom AI tool was bought before the rulebook was finished. Upstream sits Alaska's Strategic Framework, Artificial Intelligence for K-12, issued by the Department of Education and Early Development, which means what Kenai adopts previews what other Alaska districts face.

Status: pending decision. Decided by Kenai Peninsula Borough School District Board of Education.
Public access: indirect. An elected school board decides, and its regular meetings carry a public comment period. There is no formal comment window on these documents and no published date for a final vote, so an Alaskan reaches this one through a board member or from the podium at a meeting.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/kpbsd-ai-policy-package/

## Dates

- 2026-07-06, AR 5131.9 first presented to the Policy Review Committee and postponed (milestone)
- 2026-08-03, Committee takes up AR 5131.9 with two competing drafts, and the board takes first readings on four more documents that evening (milestone)
- 2026-08-19, First student day of the 2026-27 year districtwide (milestone)
- 2026-09-14, Next regular board meeting (milestone)

## Sources

- [KPBSD E-Governance](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666), 2026-08-03
- [KPBSD E-Governance](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/666?item=10054), 2026-08-03
- [KPBSD E-Governance](https://egov.kpbsd.org/agenda/667), 2026-08-03
- [Alaska Department of Education and Early Development](https://education.alaska.gov/artificial-intelligence), 2026-08-09
- [KBBI AM 890](https://www.kbbi.org/2026-07-08/proposed-school-district-ai-policies-target-academic-honesty-student-privacy), 2026-07-08
- [KDLL 91.9 FM](https://www.kdll.org/local-news/2026-08-03/school-board-considers-classroom-screen-time-limits), 2026-08-03

## How this decision moved

**2026-08-09** Tracked. Verified against the district's own agendas and the posted policy drafts. AR 5131.9 sits under Policy Review-Ongoing on the August 3rd committee agenda after being postponed on July 6th, and two versions are attached, one from Administration and one from board member VanBuskirk. The Administration draft makes misuse of AI tools a violation of academic honesty subject to discipline under BP 5144. A separate pair, BP 6161.5 and AR 6161.5 on high-quality instruction and purposeful use of technology, came to the same meeting as new business and caps routine instructional technology at 15 minutes a day in kindergarten and first grade, rising to 90 in fourth and fifth, while stating that routine daily technology limits are not established for secondary schools. Those two documents never mention artificial intelligence. No committee minutes for August 3rd are posted, so no outcome is recorded here.
**2026-08-13** Checked and unchanged. AR 5131.9 Academic Honesty still sits under ongoing policy review on the August 3rd committee agenda, item 10054, with no action recorded since. The first student day districtwide is August 19th.

# An 89 million dollar federal grant for a coal plant in the Susitna watershed

> The Department of Energy selected Terra Energy Center Corporation of Anchorage, an affiliate of Flatlands Energy, for an 89 million dollar grant to study a 1,250 megawatt coal fired power plant west of Skwentna, with a 60 mile pipeline carrying its carbon dioxide to Beluga for injection into a depleted gas reservoir. The money funds a viability assessment rather than construction, and Terra must match it.

Status: pending decision. Decided by U.S. Department of Energy made the selection; the plant itself needs state and federal permits nobody has applied for yet.
Public access: closed. The grant selection carried no public comment period. Comment rooms open later, when the mine, the plant, the pipeline and the injection well each need their own permits.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/terra-energy-center-doe-grant/

## Dates

- 2026-06-04, Federal grant selection announced (milestone)

## Sources

- [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/business-economy/energy/2026/06/04/trump-administration-selects-proposed-coal-project-for-89-million-grant-in-susitna-river-watershed/), 2026-06-04
- [U.S. Department of Energy](https://www.energy.gov/arctic/alaska-funding-awards), 2026-08-06

## How this decision moved

**2026-08-06** Tracked, with two figures corrected against the reporting. A reader described this as an 89 million dollar grant to Flatlands Energy for a 400 megawatt plant. The recipient named is Terra Energy Center Corporation, an affiliate of Flatlands, and the plant described is 1,250 megawatts. It belongs on this docket because Railbelt power is what the region's data center proposals are competing for, and because of how far it is from being real. There is no finalized design, no permitted coal mine and no signed power purchase agreement with any utility, and the site sits more than 60 miles from the nearest transmission line. It also depends on the West Susitna Access Road, put at over a billion dollars and not counted in the project's costs. The Susitna River Coalition and the Alaska chapter of the Sierra Club have both objected.
**2026-08-12** Re-verified against the Department of Energy selection page for the coal recommissioning announcement. The award is $89 million for engineering and design of a 1,250 megawatt coal plant built as five 250 megawatt circulating fluidized bed trains, with carbon capture sized to take more than 90 percent of the carbon dioxide, an estimated 8.26 million tonnes a year. Engineering is targeted to finish in 2027 and the plant is projected operational in 2031. This money studies the plant. It does not build it.

# The executive order that lets big data centers skip the usual federal review

> Executive Order 14318, Accelerating Federal Permitting of Data Center Infrastructure, directs federal agencies to speed approvals for data centers adding more than 100 megawatts of load or costing at least 500 million dollars. It tells agencies to find and create categorical exclusions under the National Environmental Policy Act, and directs Interior and Energy to offer federal sites while Defense may competitively lease military land.

Status: watching. Decided by The President, carried out by the Council on Environmental Quality and the Interior, Energy and Defense departments.
Public access: closed. An executive order takes no public comment. Its effect is to remove review steps that would otherwise have carried one, so the room this closes is the environmental review a project would have had.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/eo-14318-data-center-permitting/

## Dates

- 2025-07-23, Order signed (milestone)
- 2025-07-28, Published in the Federal Register (milestone)

## Sources

- [Federal Register](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/07/28/2025-14212/accelerating-federal-permitting-of-data-center-infrastructure), 2025-07-28
- [The American Presidency Project](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/executive-order-14318-accelerating-federal-permitting-data-center-infrastructure), 2025-07-23
- [GovInfo, Compilation of Presidential Documents](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/DCPD-202500788), 2025-07-23

## How this decision moved

**2026-08-06** Tracked, with the number corrected. A reader asked for Executive Order 14314; that order is Making America Beautiful Again by Improving Our National Parks, and it raises national park entry fees for foreign visitors. The order that governs data center permitting is 14318, signed July 23rd, 2025. Its Alaska relevance is direct, because it instructs the Defense Department that it may competitively lease military land for qualifying projects, which is the authority underneath the Air Force offer of about 4,700 acres at Joint Base Elmendorf Richardson, Eielson and Clear that this docket already tracks. A categorical exclusion means a project is presumed to have no significant environmental effect and skips the study that would otherwise be written, so the order's practical effect in Alaska is fewer published environmental findings on the largest power users the state has ever considered.


---

# The AI ratepayer pledge, and which Alaska utilities have signed it

> The White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge asks AI companies, utilities and data center developers to commit that new data center load pays for its own generation and delivery instead of shifting the cost onto households. USA TODAY and POWER both describe it as voluntary and non binding. Gov. Mike Dunleavy signed the governors addendum on July 23, 2026, one of 23 governors. Read live on July 26, 2026 the signatory list showed a single Alaska entity, Cordova Electric Cooperative, a 1,566 customer cooperative that is not connected by transmission line to any other community.

Status: watching. Decided by Each Alaska electric utility board, including the Railbelt cooperatives.
Public access: indirect. Alaska's electric cooperatives are governed by boards their own members elect, so a member can ask their board directly whether it intends to sign. A voluntary federal pledge has no public comment docket, which is why this room is indirect rather than open.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/ratepayer-protection-pledge-alaska-utilities/

## Dates

- 2026-03-04, Pledge first signed by seven AI companies at the White House (milestone)
- 2026-07-23, Governors addendum signed, Dunleavy among 23 governors (milestone)
- 2026-07-26, Signatory list read at 281, one Alaska entity on it (milestone)

## Sources

- [The White House](https://www.whitehouse.gov/ratepayer-protection-pledge/), 2026-07-26
- [Republican Governors Association](https://www.rga.org/republican-governors-sign-president-trumps-ratepayer-protection-pledge/), 2026-07-23
- [U.S. Environmental Protection Agency](https://www.epa.gov/newsreleases/president-trump-expands-historic-ratepayer-protection-pledge-protect-american), 2026-07-23
- [POWER Magazine](https://www.powermag.com/white-house-expands-data-center-ratepayer-pledge-as-congress-moves-to-codify-protections/), 2026-07-23
- [Cordova Electric Cooperative](https://www.cordovaelectric.com/about/), 2026-07-26

## How this decision moved

**2026-07-26** Tracked. The White House expanded the Ratepayer Protection Pledge on July 23 and 23 Republican governors signed an addendum committing to implement its principles to the greatest extent possible, Dunleavy among them. The pledge itself binds signing companies to five things, build bring or buy new power supply, pay for new delivery infrastructure, pay whether they use the power or not, invest in local jobs, and contribute to grid and community resilience. Both USA TODAY and POWER describe it as non binding. A read of the signatory list on July 26 returned one Alaska name, Cordova Electric Cooperative, and no Railbelt utility.
**2026-08-06** Re-read the White House signatory list today. It still shows Cordova Electric Cooperative as the only Alaska entity on it, out of 281 listed signatories, eleven days after the last check. No Railbelt utility has signed. Chugach Electric, Golden Valley Electric, Matanuska Electric and Homer Electric are all still absent, and those are the utilities that would carry a large Railbelt data-center load. Nothing else about the pledge changed.
**2026-08-12** Re-verified against the White House page. Cordova Electric Cooperative is still the only Alaska utility on the signatory list.

# Anchorage data-center zoning ordinance AO 2026-27

> On March 27, 2026 the Anchorage Assembly adopted ordinance AO 2026-27 in a 10 to 2 vote, defining data centers in the municipal zoning code for the first time. It confines them to commercial and industrial zones, requires landscaping buffers and enclosed power equipment, and requires written statements from electric and water utilities that the grid has sufficient system capacity before a project proceeds. Members Scott Myers and Keith McCormick voted against it.

Status: decided. Decided by Anchorage Assembly.
Public access: indirect. The elected Anchorage Assembly adopted the ordinance in a public 10 to 2 vote. Residents reach it through Assembly elections and public testimony.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/anchorage-ao-2026-27-data-center-zoning/

## Dates

- 2026-03-27, Assembly adopts AO 2026-27 (10 to 2) (vote)

## Sources

- [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/alaska-news/anchorage/2026/03/27/anchorage-assembly-preemptively-adopts-data-center-regulations/), 2026-03-27

## How this decision moved

**2026-07-18** Tracked from this run. Anchorage adopted the data center land use framework 10 to 2 on March 27, the first local guardrail of its kind in the state. Sponsored by Anna Brawley and Daniel Volland. Added because Carousel No. 10 turns on whether a Railbelt data center helps or hurts ratepayers, and this ordinance is the one enacted local guardrail while the state bill stalls.

# Copper Valley Electric's shelved nuclear reactor study

> Copper Valley Electric studied putting a 10 megawatt micro modular reactor into its isolated Glennallen and Valdez system, which is connected to no other utility and burns liquid fossil fuel for roughly a third of its power. The cooperative finished a pre feasibility study, published it, and then tabled the project indefinitely.

Status: closed. Decided by Copper Valley Electric Association board.
Public access: indirect. Copper Valley Electric is a member owned cooperative, so its board answers to ratepayers who elect it. The project is tabled, so there is nothing before the board to comment on now.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/cvea-micro-modular-reactor/

## Dates

- 2022-02-02, Study announced with Ultra Safe Nuclear Corporation (milestone)
- 2023-08-09, Board tables the project indefinitely (decision)

## Sources

- [Copper Valley Electric Association](https://www.cvea.org/about/project-reports/potential-micro-modular-nuclear-reactor-project.html), 2026-08-06
- [Copper Valley Electric Association](https://www.cvea.org/press/release/2022/02/02/copper-valley-electric-partners-with-ultra-safe-nuclear-corporation-on-feasibility-study-of-micro-modular-reactor-energy-system.html), 2022-02-02
- [World Nuclear News](https://www.world-nuclear-news.org/articles/ultra-safe-nuclear-corporation-files-chapter-11-petition), 2024-10-30

## How this decision moved

**2026-08-06** Added as a closed item, because a reader asked for its approval timeline and there is none. The cooperative's own project record is headed that the micro modular nuclear reactor project was tabled indefinitely, dated August 9th, 2023, and the completed pre feasibility study is posted publicly beside it. The study partner, Ultra Safe Nuclear Corporation, filed for Chapter 11 on October 29th, 2024, and its micro modular reactor business was sold to another company in December 2024. Recording it here rather than leaving it out, because what a utility considered and shelved is part of the record, and a reader looking for this timeline deserves to find the answer rather than nothing.

# HB 259, state utility standards for large data centers

> HB 259, introduced by Rep. Donna Mears in January 2026, would have set utility rate-setting guidelines and community benefit agreement standards for large energy use facilities such as data centers, and given the Regulatory Commission of Alaska new duties over them. The House Energy Committee heard it twice, on January 29th and February 3rd, 2026, taking testimony from Greensparc, GCI, the Alaska Municipal League and former Rep. Paul Seaton. It never advanced out of that committee, and it carried a second referral to House Community and Regional Affairs it never reached. The bill died with the 34th Legislature at sine die on May 20th, 2026. Alaska still has no statewide cost-allocation rule governing how a large data-center load is billed against other ratepayers, which leaves that question with the Regulatory Commission of Alaska and with individual utility boards.

Status: closed. Decided by Alaska Legislature (House Energy Committee).
Public access: closed. The bill died when the Legislature adjourned. No public path remains to this vehicle. A constituent who wants these standards has to ask a legislator to introduce them again in the 35th Legislature, which convenes in January 2027.
Canonical: https://alaskaaihq.com/docket/hb-259-data-center-utility-standards/

## Dates

- 2026-01-20, Prefile released, read the first time, referred to House Energy then Community and Regional Affairs (milestone)
- 2026-01-29, First House Energy Committee hearing (milestone)
- 2026-02-03, Second House Energy Committee hearing, last recorded action on the bill (milestone)
- 2026-05-20, 34th Legislature adjourns sine die, the bill dies in committee (milestone)

## Sources

- [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/alaska-news/anchorage/2026/03/04/data-centers-powering-the-ai-boom-demand-local-energy-anchorage-assembly-members-want-to-regulate-them/), 2026-03-04
- [Alaska State Legislature](https://www.akleg.gov/basis/Bill/Detail/34?Root=HB+259), 2026-01-20
- [Anchorage Daily News](https://www.adn.com/politics/alaska-legislature/2026/05/21/alaska-legislature-adjourns-with-eye-toward-special-session/), 2026-05-21

## How this decision moved

**2026-07-18** Tracked from this run. The state level counterpart to the Anchorage ordinance, HB 259 would set rate-setting and community benefit standards for big loads but sits in the House Energy Committee. Its stall is the policy gap at the center of Carousel No. 10, no statewide rule decides whether a data center spreads or shifts costs onto households.
**2026-08-06** Correction. This entry showed HB 259 as pending a decision. It is not pending. The bill died in the House Energy Committee when the 34th Legislature adjourned sine die on May 20th, 2026, and this tracker carried the wrong status for the eleven weeks since. Re-verified today against the Legislature's own bill record, which shows the last action on February 3rd, 2026 and no action after it, and against Anchorage Daily News reporting that lawmakers introduced 683 bills in the two-year cycle and passed 111. HB 259 was not among them. Status moves to closed. Two facts this entry had never recorded are now here, that the committee actually heard the bill twice and took outside testimony, and that it carried a second referral to House Community and Regional Affairs that it never reached.
